The article compares the Michael Brown shooting in Ferguson and the Walter Scott shooting in North Charleston, noting that while both involved a white officer and an unarmed black victim, the Scott case had a clear video evidence of him fleeing when shot, leading to swift charges against the officer. It highlights that the stark divide over justification seen in Ferguson did not emerge in the Scott case, and suggests the visual evidence may have prevented the prolonged unrest and speculation that followed the Brown shooting. Additionally, the article points out demographic differences between the two cities' police forces and populations, though both remain disproportionate.

At least five people were killed and thousands fled to temporary shelters in Durban, South Africa, following mob attacks on immigrants with machetes. Aid groups report that the violence, fueled by accusations that foreigners are taking local jobs, has displaced roughly 8,500 people, with fears the unrest could spread to other regions like Johannesburg.

The article details the suspicious deaths of individuals who died under questionable circumstances while in police custody. It highlights the case of Freddie Gray, who died a week after sustaining a severe spinal cord injury during his arrest, and another case involving a man who was found dead in a police car despite being handcuffed and frisked. Both cases have sparked public outrage and investigations into the circumstances surrounding the deaths.

A woman in Georgia was arrested after posting a Facebook threat to "shoot every white cop in the nation," using a fake name to conceal her identity. Authorities, including the FBI and local police, traced the post to Ebony Dickens, who was charged with disseminating information related to terrorist acts and held on a $10,000 bond.

In November 1942, the SS City of Cairo was sunk by a German U-boat while carrying 100 tons of silver coins from India to England; the wreck was discovered in 2011 and the silver was recovered in 2013, with the UK Treasury selling the coins at a value of approximately $50 million at current rates.

A jury of 12 regular members and 12 alternates has been selected for the trial of James Holmes, the suspect accused of killing 12 and injuring 70 in the 2012 Aurora movie theater shooting. The selection process, which began in January with nearly 9,000 potential jurors, concluded after months of intensive questioning, with opening statements scheduled to begin on April 27. Holmes, who has pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity, faces 165 charges and the possibility of a death sentence if convicted.

Tickets for the Mayweather-Pacquiao fight are selling at extreme prices, with ringside seats reaching up to $180,000 on secondary markets. While the high cost reflects the event's massive demand, Bob Arum notes that wealthy fans are willing to pay any price to attend.

Two audio recordings from the aftermath of the Walter Scott shooting have emerged, capturing former officer Michael Slager's demeanor and a phone call with his wife. In the recordings, Slager appears to downplay the incident while discussing the situation with colleagues, even as he faces murder charges for shooting the unarmed Scott as he fled. If convicted, Slager could face life in prison or the death penalty, though the latter is considered unlikely given the lack of statutory aggravating circumstances.

Robert Boardwine was granted joint legal custody and visitation rights over his son after a Virginia appeals court ruled that a turkey baster does not constitute "medical technology," thereby disqualifying Joyce Bruce's claim that Boardwine was merely a sperm donor. The court determined that Boardwine, who provided the sperm, is the biological father and is legally entitled to be part of his child's life, despite the unconventional method of conception.

Jurors in the Boston Marathon bombing trial deliberated for over seven hours on Tuesday but have not yet reached a verdict, sending two questions to be addressed Wednesday. Dzhokhar Tsarnaev, 21, faces life in prison or the death penalty for setting off a bomb that killed three people and injured hundreds at the 2013 race. The prosecution emphasized Tsarnaev's intent to terrorize civilians, while the defense argued he was merely following his deceased older brother's lead.

Protesters rallied in Baltimore following the death of Freddie Gray, chanting "No justice! No peace!" and marching to a local police station. The demonstration remained largely peaceful, though one man was arrested after crossing a barricade, as family members and community leaders called for accountability and healing.

Third-grade teacher Kyle Schwartz asks her students to complete the sentence "I wish my teacher knew..." to build trust and reveal their needs. The assignment often uncovers difficult home lives, loneliness, and big dreams, fostering a safe space for students to share what they're comfortable with. Schwartz shares these anonymous notes on Twitter, inspiring other educators to try the exercise and support her classroom through DonorsChoose.org.

Officer Michael Slager was fired and charged with murder after a video surfaced showing him shooting Walter Scott in the back as he fled a traffic stop. The incident has sparked national outrage and protests, drawing comparisons to the Michael Brown case in Ferguson. Authorities are investigating the shooting, and the city has moved to equip all officers with body cameras.

The University of Nebraska at Omaha is investing $81.6 million in a new arena, but the biggest buzz isn't about the facilities—it's a taco cannon. A local taco shop has partnered with the university to launch foil-wrapped tacos into the stands during events, proving that while the food might arrive less than "restaurant quality," it is definitely "edible." The viral idea, which has taken over social media, will officially debut when the new stadium opens this fall.

A Japan Railway maglev train set a new world speed record of 603 km/h (374 mph) on Tuesday, breaking its own record from the previous week. The train covered 1.8 kilometers in just 10.8 seconds while traveling above 600 km/h, showcasing the potential for high-speed rail travel between Tokyo and Nagoya in the future.

Charlotte Dujardin cemented her status as a dressage legend by winning her second consecutive World Cup title with Valegro, narrowly missing her own world record but dominating the competition. The Las Vegas event also saw rising stars like 19-year-old Bertram Allen secure a bronze medal in show jumping, highlighting a successful weekend for younger riders alongside established champions.

The world's top showjumping and dressage horses have arrived in Las Vegas for the World Cup Finals, transported in "business class" via Qatar Airways from Amsterdam. The event, held at the Thomas & Mack Center, aims to elevate the sport's profile in the U.S. with a $8 million budget, celebrity appearances, and an atmosphere blending high-stakes competition with Vegas showbiz.

An Israeli man, Ronen Ziv, is stranded in Israel awaiting the birth of his child via surrogate in Kathmandu as a devastating earthquake ravages Nepal. He fears his surrogate mother, Nafisa Shaje, cannot access proper medical care for a safe delivery due to the chaos and overwhelmed hospitals. Ziv is working with officials to evacuate Shaje to Israel, worried that without intervention, the birth could become a catastrophe.

In 1944, 16-year-old Yong Soo Lee was among over 200,000 women from across Asia who were kidnapped and forced into sexual slavery by the Japanese Imperial Army. As Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe prepares to address Congress, advocates urge him to issue a clear, unequivocal apology and accept historical responsibility, noting that his government has continued to deny and distort the historical record despite previous resolutions and international reports acknowledging the atrocities.

Chad Bernstein's nonprofit, Guitars Over Guns, provides free music instruction and mentorship to at-risk middle school students in Miami's poorest communities, helping them improve academically and stay in school. Since 2008, the program has served over 225 students, with participants showing more than a 90% increase in academic performance and attendance. Bernstein, a professional musician, uses music as a tool to give students a sense of identity and belonging, pairing them with mentors to guide them through instrument learning and performance.

Two CNN Heroes, Anuradha Koirala and Pushpa Basnet, are among the earthquake survivors in Kathmandu, Nepal, struggling in the aftermath. Koirala's nonprofit, Maiti Nepal, has seen its rehabilitation center and hospice damaged, forcing the children outdoors and leaving them vulnerable to abuse and cholera due to lack of clean water. Meanwhile, Basnet's Early Childhood Development Center has crumbled, forcing the 45 children she cares for to shelter in a damaged greenhouse field while fearing aftershocks and lacking basic necessities.

Singleton Moms, founded by Jody Farley-Berens after her friend's death from cancer, provides practical support like housecleaning, meals, and financial assistance to single parents battling illness. Since 2006, the nonprofit has helped over 300 parents in the Phoenix area, allowing them to focus on family rather than daily struggles. The organization was inspired by the need to help parents like Michelle Singleton, who faced immense stress managing medical bills and household tasks alone.

NPR's report on Baltimore's unrest falsely claimed African-Americans were "targeting Asian-owned businesses," a narrative that has persisted since the late 1980s. However, experts argue this is a misleading distraction that shifts blame from structural inequality to inter-minority conflict. Instead of racial animus, the damage to Asian businesses appears to be collateral from violence in economically vulnerable neighborhoods.

Jordan Spieth won the Masters by equaling Tiger Woods' record low score, becoming the second-youngest champion in history. He dedicated his victory to his autistic sister Ellie, who could not attend, saying she provides him with perspective on what truly matters in life.

Louis Jordan, 37, was rescued after 66 days adrift in the Atlantic Ocean following a capsizing incident off the South Carolina coast. His father, Frank Jordan, expressed immense relief, crediting his son's survival to his strong constitution and prayers. The younger Jordan survived by rationing limited supplies and ingeniously using his laundry to attract fish.

In 2003, less than 30% of religiously affiliated Americans supported same-sex marriage, but by 2014, support had risen to 47%, surpassing opposition for the first time. This dramatic generational shift has led major religious groups to file amicus briefs in support of marriage equality as the Supreme Court prepares to rule on the issue in *Obergefell v. Hodges*.

California Governor Jerry Brown has implemented the first-ever mandatory statewide water restrictions in response to a severe, four-year drought, acknowledging that the state's outdated water infrastructure cannot sustain current growth. The measures are seen as a critical step toward long-term reform, especially as the drought is linked to broader global water scarcity and climate change risks that threaten regions like the Indian subcontinent and Syria. While temporary, the restrictions highlight the urgent need to rethink water allocation to adapt to a drier future.

Millennials are increasingly prioritizing personal happiness and career over traditional marriage, with many viewing it as optional rather than necessary. A Pew Research report found that half of young adults are "OK" with society prioritizing other goals over marriage and children, reflecting a shift toward individual fulfillment. While economic and religious concerns persist, the trend suggests a future where marriage is chosen for love and compatibility rather than social expectation.

Anthony Sideri, a 25-year-old heroin addict, hit rock bottom when he robbed a bank in a desperate attempt to fuel his addiction while withdrawing in a jail bathroom. After that harrowing experience, he achieved sobriety and now reflects on his past drug use as a thing of the past, having transformed from a high school athlete into someone unrecognizable due to substance abuse.

The migrant crisis has intensified in Sicily, where hundreds have died crossing the Mediterranean in the past 10 days, drawing global attention to a problem that has been brewing for years. With projections of up to a million migrants potentially arriving in Europe this year, Italian officials and residents are divided, as some regions refuse new arrivals while others argue the country must keep its doors open. Mayor Enzo Bianco warns that Europe must share the burden, stating that ignoring the crisis will only lead to more tragedies at sea.

NASA's Messenger probe crashed into Mercury on Thursday after an 11-year mission, ending its orbit around the sun's closest planet. The spacecraft ran out of fuel and impacted the surface at roughly 8,750 miles per hour, but not before providing valuable data on Mercury's composition and confirming the presence of polar ice. Though the mission concluded, scientists will spend years analyzing the probe's findings, and Mercury remains visible in the night sky until the end of May.

Chile's Calbuco Volcano erupted twice this week, prompting evacuations of over 4,400 residents and 2,000 additional people in Chamiza due to rising river levels and ashfall. Authorities have established a 12-mile exclusion zone and issued red alerts for tourist towns, warning of potential further activity and contamination as ash spread into Argentina.

Erica Kinsman, a former Florida State student, has filed a civil lawsuit against Heisman winner Jameis Winston, accusing him of rape and sexual battery that occurred in December 2012. While a prosecutor previously declined to bring criminal charges, Kinsman's attorney stated the lawsuit aims to clear the "false accusations" through the legal system as Winston prepares for the NFL draft.

The Italian Coast Guard ship Calabrese patrols the Mediterranean off Lampedusa, a primary entry point for migrants crossing from Africa. During a routine patrol, the crew encountered a small boat carrying migrants but determined it was empty, as it was "riding high" in the water. The mission highlights the crew's ongoing efforts to distinguish between smuggling vessels and those in distress, following tragic events like the 2013 shipwreck that claimed over 350 lives.

According to a South Korean lawmaker briefed by the National Intelligence Service, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has executed approximately 15 senior officials this year for minor infractions or dissenting views. The intelligence suggests Kim rules with an iron fist, punishing those who challenge his authority, such as a Ministry official executed for criticizing the forestry program and musicians killed over a scandal.

Taylor Swift revealed on Thursday that her mother, Andrea Swift, has been diagnosed with cancer. The singer asked for privacy regarding her mother's condition but urged fans to ensure their own parents get screened, hoping an early diagnosis could lead to an easier battle.

At least two people were detained in Baltimore as protesters scuffled with police over the death of Freddie Gray, who died a week after sustaining a severe spinal cord injury during his arrest. While the demonstrations were largely peaceful, tensions rose as demonstrators marched to a police station and surrounded vehicles, frustrated by the lack of information regarding Gray's death and a police union's comparison of the protests to a "lynch mob."

Bikram Choudhury, the founder of "hot yoga," has faced renewed scrutiny after six former students accused him of rape and sexual assault. In a recent interview, Choudhury denied the allegations, claiming the women were manipulated by lawyers, while his accusers argue he has lied to protect his reputation. With civil lawsuits pending and studios distancing themselves from his name, the future of the Bikram yoga brand hangs in the balance.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi are steering the world's two most populous nations, with Modi recently celebrating India's Mars mission and promoting "Make in India" to accelerate economic growth. While Modi's India aims to become a fast-growing economic powerhouse, China's economy is slowing after decades of rapid expansion, and experts argue India still faces significant infrastructure and education gaps before it can overtake China's manufacturing might.

The U.S. military has successfully tested "smart bullets" that can steer themselves to moving targets, allowing even novice shooters to hit their mark with extreme accuracy. Developed by DARPA's EXACTO program, the .50-caliber projectiles use optical sensors to adjust their path mid-air, significantly improving sniper range and troop safety.

Sarah Brady, a prominent gun control advocate, died Friday at age 73 from pneumonia. She dedicated her life to preventing gun violence following her husband James Brady's assassination attempt in 1981, helping secure landmark legislation like the Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act.

Kenyan Deputy President William Ruto has demanded the United Nations relocate over 600,000 refugees from the Dadaab camp to Somalia within three months, threatening to do it himself if they refuse. The request follows the Garissa University College attack, which the Kenyan government attributes to Al-Shabaab leader Mohamed Mohamud, who they allege operates within the Dadaab complex. Saudi airstrikes targeting a military base in Ibb province hit a nearby school, killing at least three students and injuring several others. The officials stated the school was not the main target, located just 500 meters from the base, but the attack highlights the increasing danger to civilians caught in the crossfire of the ongoing conflict. The incident adds to the rising death toll, with UNICEF reporting at least 74 children killed since the fighting began on March 26.

Izzat Ibrahim al-Douri, a former top deputy to Saddam Hussein and key figure in Sunni extremist groups, was killed in a security operation in the Hamrin Mountains. Iraqi officials and Shia militia confirmed his death, noting he was the highest-ranking member of Hussein's regime to evade capture since 2003.

The Solar Impulse 2, a solar-powered plane attempting a round-the-world journey, has been grounded in Chongqing, China, for over two weeks due to unfavorable weather conditions. Pilots Bertrand Piccard and Andre Borschberg are waiting for cross winds to drop below 4 knots before they can resume their flight, which has already been delayed by technical and environmental setbacks. Despite the layover, the team remains eager to continue, viewing the delay as part of the adventure of flying with the forces of nature.

ISIS has established a bureaucratic system in its controlled territories, issuing official documents for matters like birth certificates and vaccinations while enforcing a strict interpretation of Islamic law. The group has reopened institutions like Mosul University under a new curriculum that bans subjects such as democracy and archaeology, and while girls are allowed to attend school, education is segregated and governed by Sharia guidelines.

Five Chinese feminist activists were released on bail after being detained before International Women's Day for planning a campaign against sexual harassment. While their release was welcomed, lawyers and supporters emphasized that the women remain under investigation and face ongoing restrictions, highlighting the precarious state of China's legal system. The incident drew international condemnation, with U.S. officials urging China to support rather than silence the activists.

A Columbia University student is suing the school after he was accused of rape but cleared in a disciplinary hearing. The lawsuit alleges the university allowed his accuser to publicly brand him a "serial rapist" and institutionalized her harassment by supporting her senior thesis project, "Carry That Weight." Nungesser claims the school violated his right to an education free of discrimination by failing to protect him after his name was cleared.

President Obama and Cuban President Raul Castro held a historic handshake at a dinner in Panama City, marking the first high-level U.S.-Cuba contact in over five decades. The meeting signifies a major step toward normalizing relations, with Obama expected to remove Cuba from the U.S. terrorism list during the Summit of the Americas.

Joseph Kent, a community activist, was arrested live on CNN during a curfew in Baltimore while attempting to de-escalate tensions. His attorney confirmed he was released from jail and stated Kent wanted to make it clear he does not condone violence. Investigators have since made 10 arrests, with seven charged with curfew violations.

SpaceX successfully launched a cargo Dragon spacecraft to the International Space Station, but failed to land the rocket's first stage on a floating barge, which tipped over upon impact. Elon Musk stated the rocket landed hard but survived the initial impact, marking the second attempt after a scrubbed launch due to weather. The mission aims to deliver over 4,300 pounds of supplies and equipment to the station, with SpaceX continuing to pursue reusable rocket technology to reduce costs.

The Supreme Court heard historic arguments on the constitutionality of same-sex marriage, with Justice Anthony Kennedy widely seen as the pivotal vote. While Kennedy signaled sympathy for same-sex couples by questioning the definition of marriage and the ability to procreate, Chief Justice Roberts and conservative justices expressed concern that legalizing gay marriage would close off democratic debate at the state level.

The death of Freddie Gray in Baltimore has sparked protests over police brutality, though the exact cause of his severe spinal cord injury remains unclear. While Gray was arrested on a weapons charge and appeared able-bodied when placed in a police van, he became unresponsive during transport and later died, leading to the suspension of six officers involved in his arrest.

The United Nations has appealed for $174 million to assist Nigerian refugees fleeing Boko Haram attacks into neighboring countries, where over 192,000 people are currently displaced. The agency warns that displaced people are unable to return home and face severe needs, including lack of education and mental health support, with thousands of children out of school and some forcibly recruited by militants. The funding aims to support 23 agencies providing essential aid such as clean water, shelter, and protection to both refugees and the 1.2 million people already displaced within Nigeria.

A Michigan man was cleared of all charges after a traffic stop video showed an officer punching him while he was on the ground. The officer involved, William Melendez, was charged with assault and mistreatment of a prisoner, while the police chief resigned amid the controversy. The motorist, Floyd Dent, expressed relief, stating the justice system was working, though the officer's lawyer maintains the video does not tell the full story.

The U.S. Navy is developing unmanned drone ships to counter the expanding submarine capabilities of China and other nations, aiming to maintain underwater dominance through advanced detection. Initiated by DARPA, the Anti-Submarine Warfare Continuous Trail Vessel (ACTUV) is designed to independently track quiet diesel-electric submarines over vast distances at a fraction of the cost of manned warships. The program aligns with the Navy's push to integrate unmanned systems as the "new normal," with prototypes already in production and potential deployment by 2018 if testing succeeds.

Nobel laureate Günter Grass, the acclaimed author of "The Tin Drum," died at age 87 in Lübeck. His work, which often explored the moral complexities of war and the history of his hometown Danzig, sparked controversy in his later years over his past service in the Waffen SS and his criticism of Israel.

Feidin Santana, who recorded the fatal shooting of Walter Scott by Officer Michael Slager, revealed he was told by another officer to stop filming but continued anyway. His video, which contradicted the officer's initial account, provided crucial evidence leading to Slager's firing and murder charge. Santana stated he came forward partly to protect himself from retribution, believing Scott was unarmed and fleeing when shot.

A magnitude-7.8 earthquake struck near Kathmandu, Nepal, causing widespread destruction and killing over 1,800 people. The disaster has left entire neighborhoods in rubble, triggered avalanches on Mount Everest, and prompted a massive international rescue effort as the death toll continues to rise.

A former Japanese school principal was arrested in the Philippines for allegedly paying for sex with over 12,000 women, including minors as young as 14, during visits spanning 25 years. Police seized over 147,000 photos from his possession, and he now faces criminal charges for producing child pornography and obscene acts.

A Franklin County grand jury indicted nine members of a criminal syndicate for stealing and trafficking high-end bourbon from Buffalo Trace and Wild Turkey distilleries. The alleged ringleader, Gilbert "Toby" Curtsinger, a 20-year Buffalo Trace employee, was arrested after police found stolen bourbon barrels on his property. While authorities allege Curtsinger distributed stolen Pappy Van Winkle through his softball league, his mother maintains he knows nothing about the rare whiskey.

Thousands of Brazilians protested across major cities on Sunday, demanding the impeachment of President Dilma Rousseff amid a massive corruption scandal involving the state oil company Petrobras. Police estimated 275,000 demonstrators marched in Sao Paulo alone, chanting "Out with Dilma" and waving Brazilian flags while singing protest songs from the nation's past. While Rousseff denied any involvement in the kickback scheme and her supporters call her position merely a figurehead, protesters argue her tenure is untenable given her role as Petrobras chairwoman during the alleged corruption.

Baltimore police acknowledged that Freddie Gray did not receive timely medical care and was not buckled into a seat belt during his transport, with Commissioner Anthony Batts stating there are "no excuses" for the failure to secure him. Investigators are examining the van's three stops, including one where Gray was seen on the floor asking for a medic before he suffered a severe spinal cord injury and died a week after his arrest. While the family's attorney called the admissions a step toward truth, they emphasize the central unanswered question remains: why Gray needed medical attention in the first place.

In 2001, the Taliban destroyed ancient Buddha statues in Afghanistan, prompting Iraqi engineer Ben Kacyra to found CyArk in 2003. The non-profit uses laser scanning technology to digitally preserve at-risk historical sites, ensuring that accurate replicas survive even if the physical structures are lost to conflict or disaster. To date, CyArk has scanned over 200 World Heritage sites, including Mosul and Pompeii, creating a digital archive intended for future reconstruction and education.

The bison walked about a mile and crossed the Innoko River before reaching the grass meadows of Lower Innoko, which are surrounded by the Yukon River.

He added that he was six-under par through eight holes, but then hit two balls into the water on the ninth hole.

Jack Grealish has a message for Premier League referees: stop telling him to pull up his socks. The Aston Villa teenager is famous for wearing his socks high over his shinpads. He says he will keep doing this because it is a superstition he has had since he was a child.

Tim Bresnan thinks a strong start to the season with Yorkshire could help him get back into the England Test team. He hasn't played for England since they lost the Ashes 5-0 in Australia in 2013/14. However, he recently trained with the team in Australia and played for England Lions in South Africa. Last year, he was very important to Yorkshire winning the championship. He took 30 wickets and scored 95 runs in the match that decided the title.

Stuart Broad avoided a serious injury. Jonny Bairstow scored 98 runs but fell short of making a century against his own teammates. Meanwhile, England's test warm-up match at Lord's was more important than a practice game at Warner Park, where four touring players joined the local side. Jonathan Trott scored nothing, and Gary Ballance scored 17, but Joe Root finished the day not out on 87. England ended the day at 303 for nine wickets.

Everton is near the bottom of the Premier League, but almost 4,000 fans still came to watch the team train at Goodison Park on Tuesday. The club held the open session during the school half-term holiday to get ready for their game against Swansea City on Saturday. Fans could watch the team for free, and players John Stones and Aaron Lennon stayed afterward to meet people at the club store.

Steve Parish, the chairman of Crystal Palace, wants to get more money to improve Selhurst Park, the team's home stadium. This comes after the team beat Manchester City 2-1 on Monday. There have been reports that Josh Harris, an American businessman who owns other sports teams, might try to buy the club. However, Parish, who saved the club from financial trouble in 2010, said he wants to stay involved and prefers getting new investment rather than selling the club completely.

Jack Grealish wants to change his memories of Wembley Stadium. As a fan, he visited twice as a teenager, but Aston Villa lost both times—once in the League Cup final and once in the FA Cup final. Now 19, Grealish has started playing for the team. He made his first Premier League start in a 3-3 draw against Queens Park Rangers, and he hopes to keep his spot for the semi-final on April 19.

Julian Speroni has signed a new one-year contract with Crystal Palace, keeping him at the club for a 12th season. The goalkeeper, who joined from Dundee in 2004, triggered the extension this week. At 35 years old, Speroni has been a key player for Palace in their fight to stay in the Premier League. He made a desperate dive to save Yaya Toure's shot in a recent game. At the end of the season, he will play a testimonial match against his former club, Dundee.

Leicester City needed a win to stay in the Premier League. Andy King scored in the 86th minute to give them the victory. The atmosphere at the King Power Stadium was very tense. Before the match, the team knew that if they did not beat West Ham, they would be relegated. After the final whistle, the players celebrated with the fans. Leicester is now only four points behind Sunderland with six games left to play at home.

Paul McShane told his Hull teammates that they need to wake up and realize they are in a relegation battle. It would have been helpful if someone had told them this before they got off the bus in Swansea on Saturday. If Hull gets relegated, which looks likely based on their remaining games, this will be one of their biggest regrets. It was a strange sight to see Steve Bruce’s players looking so lazy and uninterested in the first half against a team with nothing to play for. Paul McShane scored for Hull, but the team still lost 3-1 to Swansea on Saturday.

Haris Vuckic says he does not know where he will play next season. However, he thinks Rangers would be a good choice if Newcastle lets him leave. The 22-year-old joined Rangers on loan in January. He is the only Newcastle player on loan at Rangers who has played well, because the others are injured. Vuckic has one year left on his contract with Newcastle.

For a young man who has worked quietly in his career, the scene outside the Riverside Stadium on Monday night was symbolic. James Ward-Prowse had just led England Under 21s to a thrilling 3-2 victory over Germany, scoring the winner after a remarkable 34-pass move. He should have been surrounded by well-wishers on his way to the team bus, but on this occasion, there was peace and quiet. 'I enjoy signing autographs and giving something back to the fans,' said Ward-Prowse with a smile, 'but it was dead! There wasn’t a soul around! It was wet and windy, so everyone decided to go home.'

Tony Pulis thinks Joey Barton was right to criticize West Bromwich Albion. In December, West Brom was winning 2-0 against Queens Park Rangers, but they lost the game 3-2. Because they collapsed at the end, Barton said the players "s*** themselves" and could not handle the pressure. Pulis agrees that Barton likely had a valid point about the team losing their composure.

Manchester United player Radamel Falcao says his team's biggest threat on Sunday is Sergio Aguero. Falcao was speaking at an event for Puma shoes. He said City is a very talented team with danger everywhere, but Aguero has been very dangerous for Manchester United in the past. Aguero has scored six goals against United since he joined City in 2011.

It is that time of year when the English teams struggle in Europe because of the salary cap rules. Dai Young, the director of rugby for Wasps, has raised concerns about this every year. His team played well, pushing the French team Toulon close in a Champions Cup quarter-final match on Sunday. However, Toulon had better players. Two of the best players in the world, Matt Giteau and Juan Fernandez Lobbe, came on as replacements for Toulon. Also, two South African players, Bryan Habana and Juan Smith, were watching from the sidelines and did not play.

Tottenham Hotspur is moving forward with plans to build a new stadium on the White Hart Lane site. The club plans to open a 56,000-seat "world-class" stadium in just over three years.

To make this happen, they have started tearing down the last remaining building in the way, Archway Sheet Metal Works. The club has secured the necessary permissions and won a legal battle against a compulsory purchase order. Although Archway Sheet Metal Works fought the development in court, they lost an appeal earlier this year, and their demolition has now begun.

Reece Oxford, a 16-year-old player for West Ham, scored a header for the Under 21 team on Tuesday. He played against Manchester United, but his team lost 3-2. This goal brings him closer to making his first appearance for the senior West Ham team this season.

Gary Teale has defended St Mirren's pitch after Celtic manager Ronny Deila criticized it. Following Celtic's 2-0 win, Deila said most Scottish Premiership pitches are "terrible" and suggested artificial surfaces would be better. However, Teale argued that the criticism was unfair. He stated that he was surprised by the comments because he believes St Mirren has the best pitch in the league. Celtic midfielder Stefan Johansen scored a penalty to make the score 2-0.

Manchester United Under 21s won 2-1 against West Ham United to go four points clear at the top of the league.

West Ham took a surprise lead early when Reece Oxford headed the ball in. However, Manchester United quickly equalized when Josh Harrop scored. Joe Rothwell then scored the winning goal for United.

Adnan Januzaj was the captain for Manchester United.

Ronny Deila agrees with Gary Teale that St Mirren has one of the best pitches in the Scottish Premiership. However, he thinks this is a bad thing, not a good thing. After his team won 2-0 on Friday, Deila criticized the playing surface and suggested that artificial grass would be better at most other grounds. Gary Teale, the Buddies boss, disagreed. He said the surface is excellent and that their groundsman, Tommy, wins "pitch of the year" awards every year.

Karim Benzema called Cristiano Ronaldo a 'phenomenon' after Ronaldo scored five goals in Real Madrid's 9-1 win over Granada. It was the first time Ronaldo had scored five goals in one game. He also became only the third player to score 300 goals for Madrid, doing it in just 287 games. On Sunday, Benzema said on the club's website: 'Cristiano is a phenomenon. He always looks for goals and ways to help the team. He deserves everything he has achieved.'

Stuart McCall says his future at Rangers will not be decided until after the season ends. He has brought new energy to the club and won over the fans with three recent wins. McCall was hired last month to help the team chase promotion. Tonight, they play Queen of the South.

Louis van Gaal is known as a strict disciplinarian, but he showed his excitement when Ander Herrera scored against Aston Villa. Van Gaal had been telling Herrera to keep control of the ball before shooting. When the team went into halftime with a 1-0 lead because of Herrera's goal, Van Gaal got too emotional.

England left for the Caribbean on Thursday. They know they must beat the West Indies in a Test series starting on April 13 to save the jobs of key staff and stop rumors about Kevin Pietersen. This is very important for England because they had a bad World Cup and a new ECB chairman, Colin Graves, said jobs could depend on the results.

Christian Benteke earns £50,000 a week at Aston Villa. If the team gets relegated from the Premier League, his pay will be cut significantly. However, if he keeps scoring, other teams will be interested in him. Whether Villa stays in the league or not, his contract situation will be talked about this summer. He has two years left on his deal and wants to play in Europe. Wolfsburg have been watching him for a year, even after he injured his Achilles, and they are still looking for a new striker.

Arsenal target Paolo Dybala has said he might be playing his last games for Palermo. The 21-year-old forward has been linked with big European clubs after scoring 13 goals this season. Palermo president Maurizio Zamparini says Arsenal and Juventus have made bids for the player, who is valued at around £30 million.

Amir Khan, who was born in Bolton, spent a Friday at a safari park in northern California with his family. The 28-year-old boxer, his wife Faryal Makhdoom Khan, and their daughter Lamysa enjoyed seeing the animals. Khan posed with and fed a rare white tiger, and he also posed with giraffes and sea lions at the park.

With James Rodriguez back in the Real Madrid team, the Spanish newspaper Marca says coach Carlo Ancelotti has his "six nations" available again.

The former Monaco player has been out since early February with a foot injury. However, he has been picked to start for Real Madrid's game against Granada on Sunday.

This means Ancelotti has a strong attacking line-up of players from different countries ready to chase Barcelona in the La Liga season. The six players are:

*   **Toni Kroos** (Germany)
*   **Karim Benzema** (France)
*   **Cristiano Ronaldo** (Portugal)
*   **Gareth Bale** (Wales)
*   **James Rodriguez** (Colombia)
*   **Luka Modric** (Croatia)

Chelsea are talking about a possible tour after the season ends. This could upset many international managers. Jose Mourinho said a 12,000-mile trip to Japan is possible. No final decision has been made, but if the tour happens, the team will likely leave on May 28 or 29 for a week-long trip with two matches. Jose Mourinho did not rule out a 12,000-mile round trip to Japan for a pre-season tour. This news may worry international bosses who need Chelsea players for their mid-June friendlies and qualifiers.

Blackburn Rovers manager Gary Bowyer is angry about FA Cup rules. He cannot play 21-year-old midfielder John O'Sullivan against Liverpool in a replay on Wednesday because O'Sullivan was on loan at Barnsley when the first game was played on March 9. Bowyer wanted to include O'Sullivan, who he recently recalled from his loan, but the rules say he cannot play because he was at Oakwell during the 0-0 draw at Anfield.

Burnley manager Sean Dyche is confident his team will avoid relegation. The team is preparing for the last eight games of the season after a training camp in Spain. Some players are away on international duty, but the rest of the squad is ready. Their next match is against Tottenham on Sunday. Sean Dyche believes his team can stay in the Premier League.

Napoli president Aurelio De Laurentiis is very angry. His team has lost five Serie A games in a row. They lost 1-0 at home to Lazio in the Coppa Italia on Wednesday, going out of the competition 2-1 on the whole. Because of this bad run, Napoli fell from third place to sixth in the league. They now have a very small chance of playing in the Champions League next year.

To fix this, Mr. De Laurentiis has threatened to keep his players at a training camp for as long as he wants if they do not start playing better before the season ends.

LeBron James hurt his old team, Miami, by scoring 23 points in a Cavaliers win on Thursday. The Cleveland forward, who won two titles with Miami, helped his team beat the Heat 114-88 at the American Airlines Arena. Point guard Kyrie Irving also scored 23 points. Dwyane Wade left the game with a knee injury in the first half. Brit Luol Deng scored 17 points for Miami. With this win, Miami fell to ninth place in the Eastern Conference, behind Boston, who have the same record. LeBron James and Kyrie Irving each scored 23 points as Cleveland won in Miami.

Blackpool got relegated to League One after a 1-1 draw with Reading. However, fans were angry about the club's owner, Karl Oyston. On Easter Monday, the relegation was officially confirmed. This angered the supporters, who protested before the next game. About 45 minutes before kick-off, dozens of fans gathered outside the West Stand. They threw eggs at the directors' boxes and used flares, smoke bombs, and fireworks near the main reception area.

England captain Alastair Cook scored a century on the second morning of their opening tour match in the West Indies. He had started the day on 95 and reached 101 before retiring out. Cook scored his century with an edge to the boundary off the first ball, and later added two more runs by punching the ball from the back foot. He acknowledged his partner Gary Ballance and left the field after scoring 101 runs from 200 balls.

Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers knows his team cannot afford to lose if they want to finish in the top four. Before the international break, their 13-game unbeaten streak ended with a home loss to Manchester United. This defeat left Liverpool five points behind the teams qualifying for Europe. Losing to third-placed Arsenal on Saturday would be a major setback for their chances of returning to the Champions League next season.

This was the farthest place from the Ashes trophy possible, but a quiet day of scoring runs against weak opposition in the pretty town of Basseterre meant a lot to Jonathan Trott. It must have seemed to Trott that he would never play for England again after he got badly beaten by Mitchell Johnson during England’s failed Ashes tour almost 18 months ago. However, Trott has recovered from the mental health issue that made him leave Australia. He is now certain to start the first Test in Antigua next week as an opener. It is a great comeback.

Jacques Burger is the perfect rugby player for marketing teams to promote. He is fiercely loyal, very brave, strong, and dedicated.

Playing for Saracens, he is a favorite among his teammates but feared by his opponents. Opponents dislike him because he plays aggressively and without caution. His face is often battered and bruised from years of hard hits.

Burger says his personality changes when he plays. "I change into something else when I play rugby," he said. "When I step off the pitch I will be somebody else again. It is pretty weird."

Jose Mourinho says he does not care where Chelsea win the league, as long as they win it. Chelsea are currently six points clear at the top of the table with one game left to play. They play Stoke City at home on Saturday. Mourinho spoke at a press conference before the game. Eden Hazard will start for Chelsea after the international break.

Saturday's match against Arsenal is very important for Liverpool's chances of playing in the Champions League next season.

In December, Liverpool drew 2-2 with Arsenal. After that game, the team played well and went 13 games without losing. This put them in a strong position to finish in the top four of the Premier League.

However, two weeks ago, Liverpool lost to Manchester United. A goal from Juan Mata in that match put Manchester United five points ahead of Liverpool in the race for fourth place.

Liverpool must beat Arsenal on Saturday to keep their hopes of finishing in the top four alive.

Olivier Giroud from France won the Barclays Premier League player of the month award for March. This made him the most successful foreign player in the league's history. He scored five goals during Arsenal's four straight wins. He joined other famous French players like Thierry Henry and Eric Cantona who have won the award before.

Liverpool play Arsenal on Saturday in the early Premier League game. If past games are anything to go by, there might be lots of goals. Since the Premier League started, five hat-tricks have been scored in this match, which is more than in any other game. Their last meeting in December finished 2-2, with Martin Skrtel scoring in injury time. In 1994, Robbie Fowler scored the fastest hat-trick ever in a Liverpool vs Arsenal game.

Liverpool players Mario Balotelli, Fabio Borini, Rickie Lambert, and Lazar Markovic were surprised when YouTube star Bas van Velzen arrived at their training ground. The team thought he was a competition winner who had earned the chance to meet them and learn how to score free-kicks. However, it quickly became clear that Van Velzen was a skilled player, not just a fan, as he showed off his scoring abilities in front of the goal.

Kenwyne Jones came off the bench to score for Bournemouth in his first game. He scored just three minutes after he started playing. This happened in the 82nd minute against Ipswich.

The game was tied 1-1 at the end. Bournemouth had been losing early because of a goal by Freddie Sears. Even though Bournemouth controlled much of the match, they could not win. Jones' goal saved them from losing.

Jones had just joined Bournemouth on loan from Cardiff ten days before this game. After he scored, the Bournemouth players celebrated around him.

Australia coach Darren Lehmann defended his players after they were criticized for their behavior during Sunday's World Cup final win over New Zealand.

Wicketkeeper Brad Haddin was criticized for mocking Martin Guptill after he was bowled. A photo also showed Haddin and James Faulkner laughing at Grant Elliott after he was dismissed. Haddin clapped in Guptill's face, but Lehmann insisted this was following team orders. Lehmann also pointed out that the ICC did not punish the team, saying this proved they had not gone too far.

Rickie Fowler's girlfriend, Alexis Randock, posted a photo of herself and her sister Nicole on the beach. A mean commenter named 'fatalsplash' accused Alexis of being a "gold digger." Rickie Fowler defended his girlfriend, earning praise from his fans.

Mark Wood spent a day this week wearing his new England cricket suit. He wore it around the house a lot because he was very excited to have it on. Trying the suit on made him feel nervous and excited. Wood is one of the uncapped players in Alastair Cook’s squad. They are flying to the Caribbean on Thursday for a three-Test series against West Indies. The 25-year-old is 5ft 11in and weighs just over 12 stone. He is not the typical size or shape of a fast bowler.

England batsman Ian Bell has signed a new three-year contract with Warwickshire, keeping him at the club until the end of the 2017 season. He first joined Warwickshire in 1999 after playing for their Under-11 team. The 32-year-old has played 105 Test matches and 161 one-day internationals for England. Bell has won five trophies with Warwickshire, including the County Championship in 2004 and 2012. He said he was delighted to stay with the club.

Yorkshire has signed Indian player Cheteshwar Pujara until the end of May. They cancelled the contract of Younis Khan to make room for him. Younis was supposed to play for Yorkshire in 2015, but he is now playing for Pakistan in Bangladesh, so he cannot play for Yorkshire. Pujara will join the team as their new overseas player, but he needs a work permit first. He previously played for Derbyshire at the end of last season and scored 219 runs.

Marco Negri was a striker for Rangers who joined the team from Italy in 1997 for £3.5 million. He scored 23 goals in his first 10 league games. However, his career was hit by injuries, including one in a reserve match against Aberdeen in 2000. Negri has now revealed that he left the club because he feared he had HIV.

Raheem Sterling started a campaign called "It's Not About The Money," which took him to the Emirates Stadium. There, fans from both Liverpool and Arsenal joined together to protest the high cost of travel tickets. One banner read, "£5bn and what do we get? £64 a ticket." Despite the protest, Sterling had a tough time during the match, as Arsenal played well and defeated Liverpool.

Former All Blacks player Mils Muliaina was arrested on Friday night after Connacht lost to Gloucester. TV cameras showed him being led away by police after the game. Muliaina, who played 100 games for New Zealand, signed for Connacht this season and has played 11 times. He was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault shortly after the 14-7 loss.

On the day before his 40th birthday, John Hartson wrote about his fight against cancer. He said a serious health scare made him stop drinking so much, beat a gambling problem, and become a better husband.

In 2009, when he was 33, doctors found he had testicular cancer that had spread to his brain and lungs. Hartson wrote in the Scottish Sun that when he heard the news, he felt "as good as dead." He is a former Celtic striker.

Leeds owner Massimo Cellino says Red Bull has made a bid to buy the Championship club. Cellino, who is currently banned from football, said the majority shareholder, Eleonora Sport, is thinking about the offer. However, Leeds chairman Andrew Umbers says he does not know about any bid. He was asked about it by BBC Radio Leeds on Saturday morning.

Steven Gerrard left Liverpool at the end of the season after a great career. In 1992, before he became famous, Steve Heighway wrote a newspaper article saying Gerrard would be a success. Gerrard then moved to the USA to play for LA Galaxy. A photo from when he was 12 years old shows him as a young talent in Liverpool's academy. The 1992 article praised him, saying outstanding potential must be recognized and that Stephen Gerrard, from Huyton, could be the next great player.

A Brazilian online store says it is selling the new Chelsea kit for next season. The shirt has Gareth Bale's name on the back. The website has posted pictures of three new Chelsea kits with a "Yokohama" sponsor on the front, but they do not have the Adidas logo. It is strange, but some Chelsea fans might find it interesting that the store is selling a kit with "Bale 9" on the back. Bale has had a hard time at Real Madrid this season, and there have been reports linking him with a move back to England.

Darren Gough says he will always bat for Kevin Pietersen first. England's ninth highest wicket-taker is a loyal friend to the controversial batsman and was his best man. Pietersen has rejoined Surrey to try and get back into the England team for the Ashes this summer. He has a small chance of being picked, and everyone will watch when his campaign starts in Cardiff in two weeks.

Manchester City manager Manuel Pellegrini says his team is in a difficult position to stay in the Champions League. They have fallen behind Chelsea in the race for the title, and other teams are catching up quickly. If results go against City this weekend, they could drop down to fourth place before their game at Crystal Palace on Monday.

David Villa is happy to be playing soccer in New York for the MLS. He has started well, scoring a goal and helping his team move up to third place in the Eastern conference. On Instagram, he posted a photo of the Empire State Building with the comment, "Beautiful Empire State Building!!" The photo shows his family enjoying the famous building. His team, the newest club in the league, is currently in second place in the city, just two points behind their rivals, the New York Red Bulls. Villa wants his team to be the best in New York.

Harry Kane should skip the Under-21 European Championship this summer. Instead, he should stay with the first team for Roy Hodgson. Kane made his senior England debut last week. Although he is eligible to play for the Young Lions, Kenny Dalglish thinks he is ready for the big stage. Dalglish believes Kane should be kept fresh for the full European Championships in 2016. Kane recently scored his first England goal shortly after coming off the bench. He showed against Italy that he can handle playing against the world's best defenders.

Arsene Wenger says Arsenal must play perfectly until the end of the season to win the title. However, he believes they will be ready if Chelsea makes a mistake.

Arsenal beat Liverpool 4-1 at home, with goals from Hector Bellerin, Mesut Ozil, Alexis Sanchez, and Olivier Giroud. This result left Arsenal seven points behind Chelsea, who still have a game left to play. Up next, Chelsea will visit The Emirates in two weeks.

Wenger says his team must keep winning every game to be ready if Chelsea drops points. Despite the good result on Saturday, Wenger is not letting his team get ahead of themselves.

Consumers might soon have to pay a 10% tax on downloaded movies and music. Treasurer Joe Hockey said the states agreed to add this tax to streaming services like Netflix and Apple. The changes could also affect people buying items under $1,000 from overseas websites like Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and eBay.

No young person wants their parents following them on social media. Deion Sanders Jr., a wide receiver at Southern Methodist University, learned this the hard way this week.

On Thursday, he tweeted that he needs to get "hood doughnuts" almost every morning. He added that if the doughnuts do not come in a plain white box, he does not want them.

Seeing the tweet, his father, Deion Sanders, decided to tease him. He replied, "You're a Huxtable with a million dollar trust fund, stop the hood stuff! Lololol. Son. #truth."

A "Huxtable" is a phrase some use to refer to upper-class Black people.

Wesley Sneijder apologized after accidentally selling a knife set with Galatasaray colors on the 15th anniversary of two Leeds United fans being killed in Istanbul.

Kevin Speight and Christopher Loftus were stabbed to death before a soccer game in Taksim Square, Istanbul, on April 5, 2000. Before Saturday's Championship game between Leeds and Blackburn at Elland Road, a minute's silence will be held. However, on the morning of the match, Sneijder tweeted that his "GalatasaraySK" knife set was now available for delivery everywhere.

Arsenal beat Liverpool 4-1 at home on Saturday, moving nine points clear of their rivals. Goals from Hector Bellerin, Mesut Ozil, and Alexis Sanchez gave Arsenal a 3-0 lead before Jordan Henderson scored from a penalty for Liverpool. Olivier Giroud made it 4-1 in injury time.

Here is how the players performed:

**Arsenal:**
*   **David Ospina:** Made a great save in the second half and almost stopped the penalty.
*   **Hector Bellerin:** Played well.

**Liverpool:**
*   **Jordan Henderson:** Scored a penalty.

These amazing pictures show how this incredibly strong ant is able to tie its opposition in knots. The dramatic, up-close images were captured by a Bornean student. They show the incredible power of the tiny weaver ant. The ant is able to cleverly balance a centipede that is much larger and heavier. The centipede is ultimately helpless in the ant's grasp. Here, the centipede wraps itself in a circle as it attempts to escape.

A group of Arsenal and Liverpool fans left their seats empty at the Emirates Stadium for the first 10 minutes of their game to protest against high ticket prices. The supporters are angry about the rising cost of watching their teams, especially after the Premier League announced a huge £5.14billion TV deal. With tickets for the sold-out match starting at £64, the fans hope the empty seats will show how difficult it is for supporters to afford to follow their clubs.

Analysts at US intelligence agencies, such as the CIA and NSA, watch violent videos and photos all day to find clues about terrorists. Because this work is very disturbing, the agencies hire specialist psychologists and psychiatrists to help the analysts cope with the emotional stress.

Kurt Cobain, John Lennon, and Freddie Mercury are famous rock stars. Usually, every band has its own look. However, a company called West Coast Shaving decided to mix them together.

They took the members from 30 famous rock bands and blended their faces into one single image for each band. If you look at the pictures, some singers stand out more than others. For example, the blended image of The Beatles looks like a young Paul McCartney. Kurt Cobain is very easy to spot in the Nirvana picture, and the face of Eddie Van Halen dominates the Van Halen image.

Prosecutors are dropping almost 30 criminal cases linked to four Fort Lauderdale police officers who lost their jobs because of a racist video and text messages. The Broward State Attorney's Office reported on Thursday that they had already dropped 12 felony cases, 19 misdemeanor cases, and one juvenile case involving these officers. Nearly 20 more cases are expected to be dropped soon. The officers who made the arrests are no longer on the police force. The cases involve crimes like burglary, cocaine possession, and aggravated assault with a firearm.

A 25-year-old man named Jia Binhui has leukemia, a serious blood disease. He cannot afford hospital treatment, so he is trying a dangerous home remedy. Every day, he lies on hot coals in his garden, hoping the heat will kill the cancer cells. He believes doctors told him that heat above 42 degrees Celsius can destroy the cancer in his body.

The owner of a takeaway called Pizza Plus Fried Chicken has been fined almost £15,000. Council inspectors found mouse droppings and mouldy tomato puree at the shop in Gillingham. They also found dirty food preparation areas. The owner, Kunaratnam Kunanatha, 36, pleaded guilty to seven food safety charges at court. Inspectors saw mould growing in the tomato puree. The charges included not cleaning properly, having mice in the shop, and selling food that was not fit to eat.

Fenerbahce have asked for the Turkish league to be stopped after their team bus was shot at on Saturday. The bus was hit by gunfire as it drove to the airport after a game against Caykur Rizespor. The club said on their website that the bus driver was hurt and taken to the hospital. The driver had a cut on his head and was bleeding. The windshield of the bus was broken, and there were marks on it from the attack. The driver asked for help after the shooting.

Fran Kirby made a strong case to start in the World Cup for England Women. She helped create the first goal and scored a brilliant second goal in a 2-1 win over China.

England started strong. Kirby set up her teammate Jodie Taylor for a goal just one minute into the game. Kirby then scored her own second goal later in the match. This was only her eighth time playing for England.

Jodie Taylor celebrated her early goal. However, despite the early lead, England had trouble maintaining their attack on China's goal.

Manchester United captain Wayne Rooney scored a great goal to help his team win 3-1 against Aston Villa. The goal put United in third place in the league, above Manchester City.

United was leading 1-0 when Rooney, playing up front, spun around and hit a powerful half-volley with his right foot past the goalkeeper. It was his sixth goal in eight games for the team.

Wayne Rooney says Manchester United can still win the race for Champions League football. The team is currently fourth in the league, five points ahead of the teams chasing them. After beating Liverpool 2-1 before the break, United has a comfortable lead over the competition. Rooney believes the club is on track to qualify for the Champions League.

Mourinho and his wife Matilde were at the 2014 Victoria's Secret Fashion show in London. The Chelsea football manager says he talks to God every day, but never about football. He and his family have worked with the World Food Programme to fight hunger. He tries to keep his work and home life separate. He told the Daily Telegraph that he has a strong faith and prays to God every day.

A 16-year-old cricket fan named Jonathan Stevenson wrote a letter to Richie Benaud asking for advice on spin bowling almost 20 years ago. On Friday, Mr. Stevenson shared Benaud's reply on Twitter as a tribute after the cricket star passed away. In the letter, the 16-year-old asked for help with left-handed leg spin. Benaud wrote back with a detailed response. Mr. Stevenson, who now works as a director at LiveWire Sport, said the reply showed everything about what a great man Benaud was.

Richie Benaud, a famous Australian cricket player and commentator, died at age 84. He had been in a Sydney hospice receiving treatment for skin cancer. Benaud died peacefully in his sleep, surrounded by his wife and family. He played in 63 Test matches and was a key figure in starting World Series Cricket in the 1970s. He is remembered as a national treasure and one of Australia's most important cricketers.

Ukip's election campaign chief, Patrick O'Flynn, admitted the party can sometimes act like a "rugby club on tour," with members who are "boorish" and "chauvinistic." He said Ukip needs to "work harder" because it is "lagging" behind with female voters. He made these comments while launching the party's "policies for women" alongside Ukip deputy chairman Suzanne Evans and MEP Diane James. O'Flynn was defending the party's "blokeish" image under leader Nigel Farage.

Brendan Rodgers said Raheem Sterling's advisor is controlling him. He thinks Sterling would stay at Liverpool if he made his own choice. Liverpool lost 4-1 to Arsenal on Saturday, which ended their chance to play in the Champions League next year. Rodgers made these comments after Sterling gave a TV interview last week. In that interview, Sterling said he was flattered by Arsenal wanting to buy him.

A 23-year-old man was arrested in connection with the death of Vanessa Santillan, a 33-year-old transgender escort. Her body was found in a £400,000 flat in Fulham, south west London, at the end of March. She died from injuries to her head and neck after being strangled and beaten. The man has been bailed and told to return to a London police station for further questioning at a later date.

Chelsea had to work hard to beat Stoke 3-1 at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Eden Hazard scored from a penalty kick to give Chelsea the lead, but Charlie Adam equalized with an amazing long-range shot just before halftime. Stoke continued to pressure Chelsea until Asmir Begovic made a mistake, allowing Loic Remy to score the winning goal.

Here are the player ratings for Chelsea:

**Thibaut Courtois – 5.5**
Courtois was not busy in the first 43 minutes, but he could not stop Charlie Adam's incredible long-range shot from inside his own half.

A 22-year-old man from Wyoming stole a train from a coal mine and crashed it because he was upset about a phone call with his boss. Derek Skyler Brux pleaded guilty in January to unhitching two locomotives and driving them 13 miles down a busy track. He crashed into a stopped Union Pacific train at 10 miles per hour, backed up, and hit it again. Brux was sentenced to five years of probation and must pay $63,000 in restitution to his employer, Rail Link.

A young English cricket fan wrote a letter to Richie Benaud about 20 years ago asking for advice on spin bowling. Jonathon Stevenson was only 16 years old at the time, and he asked Benaud for tips on left-handed leg spin.

Stevenson shared Benaud's detailed reply on Twitter on Friday as a tribute after the cricket legend passed away. In his tweet, Stevenson, who is now a director at LiveWire Sport, wrote that the reply showed everything about what a great man Benaud was.

A javelin hit a judge in the heel after he tripped while trying to dodge it.

Dan Klice, 57, was working at a track meet at Ramapo College in Mahwah, New Jersey. He saw the javelin coming toward him and tried to move out of the way, but he tripped and fell. The fall left his left heel exposed, and the javelin hit him there. Klice normally lives in Olean, New York, but he traveled across the Hudson River to work the contest.

The Championship has been very unpredictable this season. It is hard to say what will happen next, but Middlesbrough is in a strong position. With only four weeks left, they are at the top of the table. The lead has changed hands 15 times already. Seven points separate the top eight teams, and there are six games left to play. Middlesbrough knows that if they keep winning, they will win the title. They are currently one point ahead of second-place Bournemouth. Their next opponent, Watford, is one point behind Bournemouth, and Norwich is one point behind Watford.

A little piglet has become famous on the internet because it learned to walk on two legs. The pig was born without back legs, but it has learned to balance using only its front legs. A video on People's Daily Online shows the young animal taking unsteady steps and wobbling around with its snout to the ground looking for food. Even though the piglet often looks like it is about to fall over, it always manages to stay balanced.

Wigan Athletic have quickly chosen a new manager. They have selected Gary Caldwell, the club's former captain, to replace Malky Mackay. The 32-year-old has been with the team since 2010. He will start his new job on Friday when Wigan plays Fulham. This appointment is a surprise because Caldwell did not expect to get the position. He lifted the FA Cup with Wigan in 2013, but now he must help the team avoid being relegated.

A cute little girl from China became an internet star because she can balance very well. In a video, she carefully puts three small bowls on her head and dances to music. She is a toddler, about two or three years old, and she spins around without dropping the bowls.

The crowd was loud and shouting. ‘Bees up, Fulham down’ came from the non-neutral end at Craven Cottage. It was a day for Brentford’s 6,000 travelling fans to enjoy. They stamped their serious play-off credentials on the Championship again, humiliating their once superior neighbours. As Stuart Dallas scored his second goal of the afternoon, boos descended on Kit Symons, who slunk back into his dugout. But this wasn’t about Fulham and their mounting deficiencies.

Peter Moores said he could work with Michael Vaughan if he gets the job of director of cricket for England. Speaking in St Kitts, Moores said it is not a personal issue. He believes England is going through a transition and needs to get strong quickly. He wants to share his ideas with the new director to help the team. Moores was not sure if England needed another voice in the dressing room.

Michael Vaughan, Alec Stewart, and Andrew Strauss are three former England captains trying to take over from Paul Downton. All three had successful playing careers and are popular figures in cricket. Sportsmail looks at the three men competing to become the most powerful person in English cricket.

**Alec Stewart (Age 52)**
*   **Current Job:** Director of cricket at Surrey.
*   **Playing Record:** He played in 133 Test matches, more than any other England player.
*   **Views:** He has a good relationship with Kevin Pietersen and believes English cricket needs to be bold.

Diego Costa might not play for at least two weeks because he hurt his hamstring during Chelsea's 2-1 win over Stoke City. The Spain international will likely miss the next Premier League games against Queens Park Rangers and Manchester United. Jose Mourinho brought Costa on at half-time after the score was 1-1. Costa limped off the field with a hamstring injury shortly after coming on. He looked upset while sitting on the turf.

Mario Balotelli was left out of Liverpool's squad to play against Arsenal. Manager Brendan Rodgers said the Italian striker had a slight injury from training. He would have only been a substitute, and was lower in the team's plans than Daniel Sturridge.

Tom Wood joked that Clermont thanked Northampton for an open training session after the English champions lost 37-5 in the Champions Cup. Northampton, who lead the Aviva Premiership by 10 points, lost in the quarter-final stage at Stade Marcel-Michelin. Clermont scored four tries to one, building a 27-0 lead by half-time thanks to their strong forwards and backs. Calum Clark and Tom Wood walked off the pitch after the 37-5 defeat. Northampton captain Dylan Hartley also led his team off the field after the crushing loss.

Robert Lewandowski returned to face his old club, Bayern Munich, as they played Borussia Dortmund at Signal Iduna Park on Saturday. Lewandowski, who left Dortmund last summer for free, scored the winning goal. This gave Bayern a 10-point lead at the top of the German league. Lewandowski spent four years at Dortmund, where he won two league titles. He scored just before halftime but celebrated quietly. You can read the full match report here.

Rory McIlroy is in an exclusive group of great golfers that includes Sarazen, Hogan, Player, Nicklaus, and Woods. He could soon join them by winning the Grand Slam at Augusta National on Sunday. Paul McGinley, the European Ryder Cup captain, says McIlroy wants to win and become the true face of golf. McGinley compares him to Jose Mourinho by saying, "McIlroy is no Jose Mourinho."

Danny Willett, a 27-year-old from England, had a great first day at the Masters golf tournament in Augusta. He played well, finishing one-under par with a score of 71. His best moment was a huge putt for an eagle at the 13th hole. His brother back home even tweeted about how well he was doing. Willett said it felt like a dream come true to start his Masters debut with an eagle and a score of 71.

Alan Stubbs said he worried that fans would cause trouble if his Hibs team made a guard of honour for Hearts. Hearts coach Robbie Neilson and defender Alim Ozturk were angry that Hibs refused to applaud the Championship winners at Easter Road. Other teams, like Rangers, Queen of the South, and Alloa, have done this. However, Stubbs said the police had not been asked, and he decided against it because he feared fighting, not because of disrespect.

Sam Allardyce is already planning for next season with West Ham. However, he is not sure if he will still be the manager. His current contract ends at the end of the season, and his future at the club is unsure. West Ham have already done better than last year by winning two more points with seven games left. However, a poor run of form in 2015 has led to speculation that he might lose his job.

Thomas Bjorn hit his second shot into the trees on a par-five hole. He played back onto the fairway for his third shot, but he aimed too far to the left. His ball flew into a crowd of people and landed in a female fan's lap. Luckily, Bjorn was allowed a free drop, and he successfully got the ball in the hole for a par. Henley is playing very well.

Ready, set... crack!

This is the moment a two-year-old boy started crying before the race even began. Video footage shows Blaine Taylor from Aberdeen, Scotland, competing against his older brother, Cody. But as Blaine went to roll his egg down a grassy hill, he accidentally stepped on it. The shell and yolk mushed into the ground.

"It's broken," Blaine exclaimed as he looked at the mess. Immediately, he started wailing with tears in his eyes. The mishap was captured on camera by his father, Luke, who posted it online. To date, the toddler's Easter egg rolling fail has been watched more than 90,000 times.

Arnold Palmer, who is 85 years old, overcame a shoulder injury to hit the opening drive at the 79th Masters. He was supposed to sit out the Par 3 Contest because of his injury, but he played anyway. Palmer hit the ball toward the ninth hole alongside Jack Nicklaus and Gary Player to start the tournament on Thursday.

Natasha Jonas was the first British woman to box in the Olympics. She is 30 years old and was born in Liverpool. She made history by fighting Katie Taylor of Ireland at the London 2012 Olympics. Jonas won bronze medals at the world and European levels. She has now retired from boxing. She said it was the right time to stop because she was injured and did not want to train full-time anymore.

Two hours before a big match, Novak Djokovic practiced his returns in an empty stadium. His hitting partner stood very close to the net to imitate John Isner's big serves. This practice helped Djokovic. He broke Isner's serve and won the match in straight sets, 7-6 (3), 6-2. After the match, Djokovic said Isner is probably the best server in tennis, but Djokovic was able to return many of his serves, which was the key to winning.

Mauricio Pochettino, a 43-year-old Argentinian manager, is seen as a hero for English football. He became famous after a controversial moment in the 2002 World Cup, where he tripped Michael Owen, leading to a penalty that David Beckham scored.

Pochettino has been in England for over two years. He is highly respected not just for his coaching, but because he gives young English players a chance to play. New research shows that he is the kind of manager young English talent wants to play for.

Nico Rosberg and Lewis Hamilton have not always agreed over the last year. However, they worked together on Thursday. Fresh from losing to Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel in Malaysia on March 29, the Mercedes teammates are trying to make sure Ferrari does not win in China. They went to the Mercedes factory in Brackley on Thursday to find a winning plan for the race in Shanghai from April 10 to 12.

Jackie Stewart, a famous Formula One driver, is sad that the German Grand Prix is gone. He is telling the sport's bosses not to give up tradition just to make money. The German race was removed from the 2015 schedule because it cost too much. The famous Italian Grand Prix is also in danger. There was confusion about which track should host the race, as it has been shared between two circuits recently. Additionally, Formula One races are starting to move away from Europe to make money in the Middle East.

Lewis Hamilton has had a very successful year with Mercedes on the track. However, he once made a mistake off the track that was very embarrassing. The 30-year-old champion has met many famous people, including politicians and celebrities. He once stepped on former President Bill Clinton's foot at Nelson Mandela's 90th birthday party back in 2008.

Work has started to fix the roof at the Silverstone motor racing circuit. The roof was damaged by strong winds on Sunday and Monday.

A part of the "Wing," a large three-story building worth $40 million (£27m), was hit by the wind. Pictures on social media showed part of the roof had been taken off.

Stuart Pringle, a director at Silverstone, says the damage will not affect upcoming events.

Two-time Formula One champion Lewis Hamilton talks about his tattoos in Men's Health magazine. The Mercedes driver, who is leading the championship after the first two races of the 2015 season, is on the cover of the May issue. In the interview, released on April 2, the 30-year-old explains the meaning behind his body art.

England World Cup winner Jason Robinson has revealed he once thought about suicide during a difficult time in his career. He was arrested for violent offences during this period.

Speaking in a documentary, the 40-year-old former player admitted he was a heavy drinker in his early days at rugby league club Wigan. This drinking almost ruined his life.

Robinson, who scored for England in the 2003 World Cup final, said he was drinking "sometimes six nights a week."

Zimbabwe might be the first test playing country to visit Pakistan since gunmen attacked the Sri Lanka team bus in Lahore six years ago. The chairman of the Pakistan Cricket Board, Shaharyar Khan, says Zimbabwe is willing to tour Pakistan for five one-day international matches. He hopes the tour will happen next month. He will meet Zimbabwe Cricket Union officials in Dubai next week and says he hopes for good news soon. Zimbabwe's limited overs captain, Elton Chigumbura, could lead the team. The Pakistan Cricket Board chairman hopes for a series of five one-dayers as soon as May.

Tim Sherwood says he is still friends with Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy. He thanked the club's board for ending his time at White Hart Lane, because that decision led to him getting the job at Aston Villa. Levy fired Sherwood as Spurs coach at the end of last season and brought in Mauricio Pochettino, ending Sherwood's five-month stay and six-year relationship with the club. However, instead of being upset, Sherwood praised Levy and the club. He will take Aston Villa to play north London on Saturday.

Alex Rodriguez played in his first game of the 2015 season on opening day. He had been suspended for 162 games because he used performance-enhancing drugs from a Florida clinic in 2014. He batted seventh and served as the designated hitter for the New York Yankees. Despite his suspension, fans welcomed him back by holding up signs that said "Forgive." His teammates also applauded as he took the field.

A new county cricket season is starting soon. The first Championship matches begin this Sunday across the country.

Yorkshire wants to keep their Division One title. Kevin Pietersen wants his runs to help Surrey get promoted from the second tier. Here is former Surrey and England batsman Mark Butcher's guide to the County Championship.

**Division One**

*   **Durham:** Mark Butcher thinks Durham will struggle to win the title. He believes they will just be happy to stay in Division One. However, they always have fast bowlers who can cause problems.

Burnley defender Michael Duff was happy with a 0-0 draw against Tottenham. He was pleased with how his team stopped Harry Kane, who was making his first start as captain. Kane could not score, and the match ended without a winner. This result helped Burnley avoid the bottom three, but it hurt Tottenham's chances of finishing in the top four.

Sportsmail looked at 10 things learned from the Premier League's Easter weekend games and the race for promotion in the Football League. 

1.  Moving Jordan Henderson from his usual central midfield position to wing back was a mistake for Liverpool manager Brendan Rodgers. In Liverpool's game against Arsenal, Henderson lost the ball 23 times in 90 minutes. He has taken over the captain's armband while Steven Gerrard is absent.
