Nedum Onuoha, a 28-year-old defender for Queens Park Rangers, is wanted by Hull City. He has 15 months left on his contract and played in a 4-1 win over West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

QPR is looking to streamline their squad, and Onuoha may leave if the team is relegated. He has also been linked with Everton and West Ham United. Additionally, QPR have held talks to sign Nicolas Spolli from Catania.

Harry Kane had a great week. He made his first appearance for the England national team and became the youngest captain in the Premier League this season. However, he will want to forget Tottenham's 0-0 draw with Burnley. Kane, who is 21 years old, was made captain after scoring on his England debut and starting a match for his country. It was a frustrating end to the week because Tottenham struggled against Burnley, a team fighting to avoid relegation. Kane called these few days the "best week of my life" after being named Tottenham captain.

Benfica have asked about Sheffield United player Diego de Girolamo. The 20-year-old Italian is leaving Sheffield United when his contract ends this summer. He also has an offer from Juventus. Celtic and Southampton are both interested in signing him. De Girolamo is currently on loan at Northampton Town.

Bobby Zamora scored a great goal for Queens Park Rangers against West Brom. He kicked the ball from far out, and it went over the goalkeeper into the net. It was a fantastic strike, probably the best of his career. This win was very important for QPR because they had lost most of their away games this season. The victory helped them move closer to safety in the league. Chris Ramsey will hope his team can keep playing well.

Andy King scored a goal in the 86th minute of Saturday's game. It was his 50th goal for Leicester City. The goal was not very spectacular; it was just a quick flick from six yards out. It happened after a scuffed shot by Jamie Vardy. The goal helped Leicester City defeat West Ham. This victory was very important for the team. King celebrated the goal with David Nugent.

West Bromwich Albion is planning to spend £3 million to sign Wales international left-back Neil Taylor this summer. Swansea City are willing to let him go, as several Premier League managers, including Brendan Rodgers and Alan Pardew, have been impressed by him in the past. However, West Brom's manager, Tony Pulis, is eager to sign the defender before a busy summer at the Hawthorns.

Leicester boss Nigel Pearson would have named Esteban Cambiasso the best player of the match, even if Cambiasso had not scored. Cambiasso scored a great goal in the 12th minute to give his team a 1-0 lead. Pearson praised the 34-year-old player, saying he is excellent even without the goal.

Daniel Agger, a defender for Denmark and Brondby, has been banned for two games. He elbowed Mattias Jorgensen in the head during a derby match against Copenhagen on Monday. The game ended 0-0, but the Danish FA disciplinary committee reviewed video footage and found Agger guilty of violent conduct.

James Tomkins hopes to play for West Ham before the season ends. However, he dislocated his shoulder in the gym last month and had surgery. He is not sure if he will be able to play again this season.

Haris Vuckic is the only player from a famous deal who got a bonus. While the other four players from Newcastle have only played 44 minutes of football total, Vuckic has done very well at Rangers. He says he would really like to stay at Rangers after this season ends. However, he has denied a report saying he wants to leave Newcastle. He still has one year left on his Newcastle contract, and talks about his future will happen this summer.

Harry Kane stood at White Hart Lane with a ball at his feet and a goal in sight. He was there to give the Tottenham fans what they wanted. However, when it was time for a crossbar challenge, he found himself in an unfamiliar position.

On Thursday morning, Kane lined up against Etienne Capoue, Nabil Bentaleb, Eric Dier, Roberto Soldado, Danny Rose, and Christian Eriksen. The fans watched as Kane tried to impress from 40 yards out. Unfortunately, he came close but ultimately missed the target.

Peter Lawwell recently admitted he told Ronny Deila it was time to get past the 'Lennie Lawrence hump.' However, the Celtic chief executive might have mentioned some local managers who had faced sadder endings. It is certain that Deila did not need to be an expert on Scottish football history to understand the pressure he was under. By late autumn, his team had lost in Europe twice, while Hamilton Academical had beaten Celtic at home. It was easy to find people criticizing him. Celtic manager Ronny Deila admitted that the first six months in charge were mentally tough.

Real Madrid have asked the referee to change a yellow card given to Cristiano Ronaldo during their 2-0 win against Rayo Vallecano. They want the punishment removed so Ronaldo can play.

Ronaldo received the card after he was fouled by defender Antonio Amaya inside the penalty area. The referee, Mario Melero Lopez, gave him the card, but Real Madrid believe it was a mistake.

Because of the card, Ronaldo is normally suspended for the next La Liga game against Eibar. However, Real Madrid are appealing the decision. The same suspension also affects Toni Kroos and James Rodriguez, who were also booked in the match.

Jeremy Peace, the chairman of West Bromwich Albion, is willing to stop the sale of the club if a deal is not finalized by July. He has received interest from groups in America, China, and Australia, some of whom have already visited the club's training facilities. Peace owns 77% of the club and is asking between £150million and £200m for it. He wants to avoid a long, drawn-out process that could disrupt the team's plans for the upcoming season. If a deal cannot be made quickly, he is prepared to wait for a better time to sell.

Rio Ferdinand thinks Louis van Gaal's choice to move Wayne Rooney back to his favourite attacking position has improved Manchester United's performance. Writing in *The Sun* before the Manchester derby, Ferdinand, who now plays for Queens Park Rangers, believes Rooney playing as a striker is the key to the team playing at their best. He praised Van Gaal for moving the captain further up the field, but he also said that the return to form of Ander Herrera, Marouane Fellaini, and Michael Carrick has been very important.

Manchester City will play Crystal Palace on Easter Monday. Glenn Murray is the most efficient striker in the Premier League this season, scoring a goal every 91 minutes on average. This is better than any other player in the top division.

Harry Kane and Diego Costa are both tied with 19 goals, putting them in a close race for the top scorer award. However, they rank fourth and fifth, behind Papiss Cisse and Olivier Giroud. Glenn Murray recently scored a penalty against Stoke City, and Harry Kane has also reached 19 goals for Tottenham this season.

In boxing, people often have big egos. A common saying is, "if he was chocolate, he’d eat himself." You might think Peter Quillin, whose nickname is "Kid Chocolate," would be full of himself. But he is not. He is facing Andy Lee next weekend, and he does not act arrogant at all.

Atletico Madrid beat Cordoba 2-0 on Saturday. This win moved them up to 62 points, putting them in third place in La Liga. Valencia is currently in fourth with 60 points. Antoine Griezmann scored Atletico's first goal in the fifth minute. He took the ball from midfield and shot it low into the corner.

Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew says he is better than many top Premier League managers. However, he has no plans to leave Selhurst Park for a team currently at the top of the table.

Since Pardew took over from Neil Warnock at the start of the year, Palace have won six out of ten league games. This has secured their spot in the Premier League for next season.

The team was in the bottom three when Pardew took over. Their climb up the table has eased fears of relegation and boosted the profile of a manager who has not yet coached a club that constantly competes for major trophies.

Billy Joe Saunders and Chris Eubank Jr. could fight each other again in less than six weeks. They got into a heated argument at a London press conference on Thursday.

The two previously fought on November 29, where Saunders won by giving Eubank Jr. his first career loss. Both men are scheduled to fight at Wembley Arena on May 9, but not against each other. Eubank Jr. will defend his WBA interim title, while Saunders will fight in a warm-up international contest before challenging for the WBO middleweight title in July.

A headline in a Manchester United magazine was very accurate. On pages 16 and 17, next to a picture of Ander Herrera, it said “Right place, right time.” However, this was not always true during his first season. From October 20 to February 17, Herrera was rarely seen and only started three of the 21 games United played. This caused a lot of talk about whether he should be in the team.

Manchester United moved up to third place in the Premier League table on Saturday after beating Aston Villa 3-1. Ander Herrera scored just before halftime, and Wayne Rooney made it 2-0 after the break. Christian Benteke scored for Villa, but Herrera scored again late in the game to secure the win for Manchester United.

Here are the player ratings from Manchester United's match:

**Manchester United (4-3-3)**

*   **David de Gea:** Had a quiet afternoon. He was partly responsible for Aston Villa's goal, which was an unusual mistake for him. He received a rating of 6.

Joey Barton told QPR to use their 4-1 win over West Brom to help them survive. QPR won the game on Saturday, ending a five-match losing streak and getting their second away win of the season. They are still in the relegation zone, but they are only three points behind Aston Villa, whom they play on Tuesday. Barton, who scored in the win and captained the team, believes they have a "hell of a chance" of staying up. QPR are currently one point behind 17th-placed Sunderland.

Anthony Joshua beat American Jason Gavern in the third round on Saturday night in Newcastle. This was Gavern's 50th professional fight. Joshua dropped Gavern twice in the second round and twice more in the third round before the fight was stopped.

Although Joshua won easily, he said he was not happy with his own performance. He was returning from a five-month break because he had suffered a stress fracture in his back.

Rangers manager Stuart McCall strongly criticized player David Templeton after Templeton complained about training methods used by previous managers Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. Templeton claimed last week that McCall had brought in new coaching and tactics that were missing before. However, McCall was not happy with the comments and suggested Templeton might be unhappy because he has not been playing much under the previous managers.

Dereck Chisora is planning a summer return to boxing. He wants to fight his British rival, David Price. Chisora has not fought since November, when he lost to Tyson Fury. He is recovering from an eye injury he got during that fight.
Dave King is back on the Rangers board. A court cleared him to return as a director. He won a large shareholder vote last month. He is now waiting for the SFA to approve him as "fit and proper."

Manchester United manager Louis van Gaal told his players that they have not yet secured a spot in the Champions League, even though they are eight points ahead of Liverpool. After a 3-1 win over Aston Villa, Van Gaal views the upcoming derby against Manchester City as a key game to finish second. He was given the job of getting the team into the top four when he took over last summer, and he is not taking anything for granted. Although Liverpool lost 4-1 to Arsenal on Saturday, putting United in a strong position, Van Gaal is not letting his team get complacent.

Barcelona midfielder Xavi will be very important for the team during the rest of the season as they try to win another treble like they did in 2009, said manager Luis Enrique.

The 35-year-old player recently went to Qatar to talk about possibly joining Al Sadd next season. He has only started five games in 21 matches this year. However, after he helped score the winning goal against Celta Vigo on Sunday, Luis Enrique believes Xavi is still very important for Barcelona's attempt to win the treble.

Celta Vigo forward Fabian Orellana has been banned for one match after he was sent off for throwing grass at Barcelona midfielder Sergio Busquets. The incident happened during Barcelona's 1-0 win over Celta on Sunday. Orellana became angry with Busquets for wasting time and threw a lump of turf at him. Busquets pretended to be hurt by the grass, grabbing his eye, even though the grass hit him on the back of the neck.

Sven Bender told his Borussia Dortmund teammates they must start scoring more goals to fix their disappointing season. The team has failed to score in four of their last five league games and currently sits in tenth place, making it very unlikely they will qualify for the Champions League. They face Hoffenheim in the DFB Pokal on Tuesday, and Bender says they need to start winning games by putting the ball in the net.

Franck Ribery says he turned down a move to Real Madrid five years ago. He was told he was as important to Bayern Munich as Lionel Messi is to Barcelona. The 32-year-old French winger has won four Bundesliga titles and a Champions League with Bayern. He claims Real Madrid wanted him after he had a disagreement with his coach, but he decided to stay because Bayern convinced him how important he was to the team.

Former Italy forward Antonio Di Natale says Alexis Sanchez is the best strike partner he has ever played with. Di Natale, who played with Sanchez at Udinese, believes the Arsenal forward is better than Neymar. He added that Sanchez is better than other Italian legends like Francesco Totti and Alessandro Del Piero.

Roma has been ordered to close part of their stadium for their next home game. This punishment happened because fans displayed an offensive banner during a match over the weekend.

The banner was shown during Roma's 1-0 win against Napoli on Saturday. It insulted the mother of a Napoli fan who was killed in clashes between supporters last year. A disciplinary committee ruled that the banner was "provocatively insulting" to the mother of an opposing fan who died in dramatic circumstances.

Hibs boss Alan Stubbs is a top candidate to become the new manager of Wigan Athletic. Mackay was unexpectedly sacked on Monday. Stubbs is currently fighting for promotion with Hibs, but he is wanted by Wigan to help them avoid relegation. Wigan are currently second from the bottom of the Championship. Previously, Stubbs' assistant John Doolan worked for Wigan manager Uwe Rosler.

Juventus kept their chance of winning three trophies alive by winning the second leg. They scored three goals through Alessandro Matri, Roberto Pereyra, and Leonardo Bonucci. This victory was impressive because the team was missing three important players: Carlos Tevez, Paul Pogba, and Andrea Pirlo. Tevez was ruled out before the match due to a thigh injury, but his absence did not stop Juventus from advancing to the final.

Several clubs are watching Aston Villa's 18-year-old defender Kevin Toner because his contract ends this summer. Norwich, Leicester, Newcastle, and Stoke have all watched him play. Villa wants to keep him and has made him a new contract offer, but other clubs are ready to sign him. Toner, who leads the Under-21 team, played against Liverpool in the FA Youth Cup.

Celtic manager Ronny Deila praised his team for winning and moving to the top of the league. He said a goal from James Forrest and a penalty from Stefan Johansen were enough to beat St Mirren. However, he was unhappy with the poor condition of the pitch. He believes bad pitches make it hard for Scottish players to improve.

Celtic's chances of winning the title look very good after they beat St Mirren 2-0 on Friday. Norway midfielder Stefan Johansen scored a penalty in the 79th minute to secure the win. Earlier, James Forrest had scored from close range. This victory gave Celtic an eight-point lead over Aberdeen at the top of the Scottish Premiership. Both teams have played 29 games, but Aberdeen can reduce the gap by playing Partick Thistle on Saturday.

Gary Player is going to his 58th Masters this week. He really hopes a new player will join an exclusive club and praised what he thinks is a great sports achievement.

The 88-year-old thinks Tiger Woods winning the career Grand Slam at age 24 was the best golf feat he has ever seen. He is very excited that Rory McIlroy might become just the sixth player to win all four majors by age 25.

Player said, "I don't think people realize how amazing it would be. When I won my Slam at 29, I told my wife that you will never see that done again."

Gene Sarazen made history with a famous shot. Ben Hogan did it with just one appearance at the Open Championship. Tiger Woods achieved it at the Home of Golf.

When it comes to completing a career Grand Slam, the stars seem to align, and it takes wonderful plays on fitting stages. Now, Rory McIlroy has the chance to join the five men who have done it at Augusta National. As Woods said, "Where better could you ask for than to complete it here?"

Rory McIlroy teed off on the first day of his practice round ahead of the 2015 Masters. He is trying to win his third major title and complete his career Grand Slam at Augusta.

Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods will play against each other on Thursday. It was not long ago that McIlroy looked up to Woods. Now, McIlroy is the world number one, which is 103 places higher than Woods. McIlroy is the favorite to win the Masters next week and get his first green jacket. Woods has confirmed he is ready to play. He is one of only five players to win the Masters, The Open, the US PGA Championship, and the US Open. McIlroy wants to be like Woods.

Barcelona coach Luis Enrique is not worried about Neymar's recent goal drought. He is confident the Brazil forward will soon return to top form as the team tries to win a second treble in a row, like they did in 2009.

Neymar has had a good season, but his form dropped after the new year. He has not scored for Barcelona in La Liga since he scored in a 5-0 win over Levante on February 15. He looked out of practice during Barcelona's 1-0 win at Celta Vigo on Sunday, where he spent much of the game arguing with the opposing fullback, Hugo Mallo.

Ian Poulter is spending a week in the Bahamas relaxing in the sun and drinking champagne. He is looking at yachts in the marina. Even though this trip sounds relaxing, Poulter says it will help him be fit and ready to play well at the Masters. He is already dreaming about winning the green jacket and what he will eat at the champion's dinner next year. He doesn't have to worry too much about the food because he is already prepared.

Manuel Pellegrini said he is not worried about losing his job, even though Manchester City's chances of winning the league took a big hit at Crystal Palace.

Palace put a lot of pressure on Pellegrini with a strong win. Goals from Glenn Murray and Jason Puncheon gave Palace the victory. This result leaves City in fourth place, nine points behind the league leader Chelsea, and they are worried about qualifying for next season's Champions League.

City fought back with a late goal from Sergio Aguero. However, the team was angry that Murray's opening goal was allowed to stand. They felt it should have been disallowed for offside and surrounded referee Michael Oliver to protest.

Former Manchester United player Quinton Fortune says Neymar looked like a shadow of his best self during Barcelona's 1-0 win over Celta Vigo. Barcelona stayed four points ahead of Real Madrid with the victory, but Fortune believes manager Luis Enrique should be worried about Neymar's performance. He claims Neymar looked uncomfortable and struggled to make an impact in the match.

Stoke City midfielder Charlie Adam scored a great goal against Chelsea. He picked up the ball inside his own half and shot 66 yards. Courtois, the Chelsea goalkeeper, ran back but could not stop the ball. Adam, a Scottish international, said the goal was the best of his career. Stoke lost the game 1-0.

Chelsea captain John Terry called Eden Hazard one of the world's best players after the Belgian helped Chelsea beat Stoke 2-1. Hazard scored a penalty to give Chelsea the lead. Stoke equalized with a 66-yard goal from Charlie Adam, but Loic Remy scored the winning goal by tapping in a pass from Hazard. This victory moved Chelsea seven points clear at the top of the Premier League.

Raheem Sterling first became famous in a TV show about Brendan Rodgers taking over Liverpool in 2012. In the show, Rodgers is seen scolding a young Sterling for talking back during practice. Now 20 years old, Sterling is a key player for England and Liverpool. On Wednesday, he was back on TV, but this time he was trying to make his own decisions. He has rejected a new contract with Liverpool and delayed talks about a new deal until the summer.

This was a disappointing result for Derby County. They were on track to win their first game in seven Championship matches against Watford, who were playing with only ten men. However, Watford’s Odion Ighalo scored an equalizer that hurt Derby’s chances of promotion.

With only fifteen minutes left, Adlene Guedioura took advantage of a mistake by Craig Forsyth. He passed the ball to his Watford teammate, who poked it past Lee Grant to get a point for his team.

Derby pushed hard at the end, spending the rest of the game attacking Watford’s box. The match ended when Heurelho Gomes made a great save to stop Richard Keogh’s header.

It has been 12 weeks since the Dundee United team confidently claimed they could win three trophies this season. Goalkeeper Radoslaw Cierzniak said, "I believe we can win all three trophies." He added, "People might laugh at me, but maybe in May we will have won the league and cups, and I will be laughing."

However, on Wednesday night against Dundee at Dens Park, those confident early January days felt like a long time ago. Cierzniak failed to hold onto the ball, allowing Greg Stewart to score the opening goal. Dundee United manager Jackie McNamara is under pressure following his team's recent poor run of form.

Tottenham wants to sign Andre Ayew from Marseille. His contract ends this summer, so he can join Tottenham for free. However, other big European clubs are also trying to sign him, and Inter Milan is leading the race to get him.

Paris Saint-Germain forward Edinson Cavani has denied rumors that he does not get along with teammate Zlatan Ibrahimovic. He says the only problem he has is being played in the wrong position. Earlier reports had suggested the pair had a bad relationship, and their coach had asked them to work better together. Cavani admits they are not close friends, but he denies there is a serious conflict. He argued with the referee during PSG's 3-2 win against Marseille.

Nick Abendanon was the only happy Englishman at the match on Saturday. After playing well for Northampton, he said he still has a small chance of being picked for the World Cup team. The former Bath player, who last played for England in 2007, scored a try and helped set up two others in Clermont Auvergne's 37-5 win. He admitted he has not ruled out playing for England again.

Paul Casey really wants to play in the Ryder Cup again. He gave up his spot on the European Tour in January to focus on the PGA Tour and try to get back into the world's top 50 golfers. His plan worked; he moved up in the rankings and is now 44th. Because he is no longer a member of the European Tour, he cannot play on the team this year. He is currently practicing for the Masters in Augusta and is very eager to get back to the Ryder Cup.

Raheem Sterling might have the power in his contract talks with Liverpool, but he should focus on playing football rather than money, says former QPR boss Harry Redknapp.

Redknapp believes Sterling is not ready for a big move to Real Madrid yet and should stay at Liverpool, where he has developed. However, Redknapp admits that if Sterling wants to leave, Liverpool will struggle to stop him. Sterling has rejected a new contract and delayed talks until the summer.

Mauricio Pochettino might have given up hope of qualifying for the Champions League, but Harry Kane won’t hear any of it. The 21-year-old, who became the youngest Premier League captain this season during the drab goalless draw against Burnley on Easter Sunday, still retains belief they can gatecrash the top-four party. Spurs are now seven points behind Manchester City, who play Crystal Palace on Monday night, with just seven games remaining. Harry Kane believes Tottenham still have a chance of qualifying for the Champions League this season. It looks a tall order, but Kane - who hailed his last few days as the ‘best week of my life’ - thinks they can make it.

Most afternoons, after the players had left Tottenham's training ground, Tim Sherwood would sit for hours with his coaches Chris Ramsey and Les Ferdinand in the staff canteen. They were always together because, in 2008, the club's chairman Daniel Levy made Sherwood responsible for the youth and Under 21 programmes. On Tuesday evening, they will be in opposing dug-outs at Villa Park. They are trying to lead their teams away from relegation danger in the final weeks of the Barclays Premier League season.

Raheem Sterling has not told his manager, Brendan Rodgers, that he wants to leave Liverpool. He is focused on playing football. Last week, Sterling gave an interview where he said he was thinking about his future at the club, but he has not yet signed a new contract. However, Rodgers says he is not worried about Sterling leaving in the summer and believes the player will stay and play for the rest of the season. Rodgers also insists that his relationship with Sterling is very strong, and that Sterling has never actually said he wants to leave.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho has added to the contract dispute between Raheem Sterling and Liverpool by saying he would sell any player who wanted to leave. Sterling, 20, wants to wait before signing a new contract with Liverpool. Chelsea and Arsenal are both interested in signing him. Sterling turned down a new offer of £100,000-a-week from Liverpool.

Michael Owen has warned Raheem Sterling that his future might not be as good as he hopes. Sterling, 20, turned down a £100,000-a-week contract at Liverpool this week. Owen, who also left Liverpool for Real Madrid in 2004, says Sterling is not ready to play in Spain yet. Several big clubs, including Chelsea, Arsenal, and Manchester City, want to sign him. However, Liverpool wants to keep Sterling, even though his current contract ends next season.

Some tour guides will do anything for a good tip. In the Australian outback, if you want to get close to a group of Emus, you need a guide who will get dirty. In a video posted by YouTube user Ratbag Nomad, a man called Australianwidefishingguide shows tourists how to do it. Emus are curious, flightless birds native to Australia. As the guide started peddling his legs slowly in the air, the mob of emus started coming closer. And closer. The video, filmed from a vehicle on an empty dirt road, shows the guide lying on his back and kicking his legs in the air to lure the emus in the distance.

Arsenal's Olivier Giroud and Arsene Wenger won the Barclays Premier League Player and Manager of the Month awards for March. Giroud scored five goals in four games as Arsenal won all four matches. This result moved Arsenal to within one point of second-placed Manchester City, with eight games left to play.

No footballer has ever been late for the start of a game because they were busy negotiating a new contract. Because of this, Raheem Sterling’s reason for ending his talks with Liverpool did not make sense. The problem is not the talking itself. The problem is the thinking. A player will not sit in an office arguing over image rights and then suddenly leave at 3:30pm. A player might worry about where he will play next season, whether at Liverpool, Arsenal, or abroad. However, waiting until the end of the season to sort this out does not help. In fact, it makes the situation worse.

Jaap Stam had just ordered a new kitchen for his home in Cheshire when he found out Sir Alex Ferguson was selling him to Lazio. The Manchester United manager did not tell Stam in the same conversation that his son, Jason, would make a lot of money as an agent in the deal. Stam’s representatives found out about this later.

On Thursday, Raheem Sterling shook hands with Liverpool boss Brendan Rodgers during training. They were at Melwood with the rest of the Liverpool squad, getting ready to play Arsenal. Rodgers is confident that Sterling will stay at the club and that the situation will be sorted out by the summer.

What if someone else said the mean things you think about yourself? Dove, a company known for helping women feel good about their bodies, decided to test this idea. For their new "One Beautiful Thought" campaign, they asked women to write down all their negative self-thoughts. The women wrote these mean thoughts in notebooks and gave them to Dove.

Two 18-month-old twin boys died after accidentally falling into a canal in Yuma, Arizona, on Friday morning.

Police and a U.S. Marine Corps helicopter searched for more than an hour before finding the boys. They were taken to a hospital, where doctors pronounced them dead.

Detectives believe the boys fell into the water by accident and do not suspect anyone of doing anything on purpose.

Paul Sturrock started his new job at Yeovil just two days after advising Torquay. On his second day in charge, Yeovil played Notts County and drew 1-1. This result meant Yeovil were relegated to a lower division.

Former US President George H.W. Bush looked healthy on Friday at a tennis tournament in Houston. The 90-year-old was hospitalized in December after having trouble breathing, but he seems to be feeling better now. Bush, who lives in Houston with his wife Barbara, is a big fan of tennis and has been to many charity events over the years.

Mark O'Meara, a 58-year-old American, made the cut at the Masters for the first time in ten years. He was one over after the first round, but played well in the second, carding a 68 with five birdies. This performance made him the third oldest player in the 2015 field, but secured his spot in the weekend's competition.

Manchester City apologized to fans and promised refunds after free coaches they provided were late and missed the start of the game against Crystal Palace. The club wrote to 300 fans who used the free ride offer for the Bank Holiday match. Because Selhurst Park is hard to reach and the game started at 8pm, many fans could not get there by train. City's Edin Dzeko and his teammates lost the match.

Advertising entrepreneur John Singleton is selling his beach house on the central coast of New South Wales. The house is located next to the Killcare Surf Life Saving Club. It is a large, five-bedroom home with views of the Pacific Ocean.

Singleton bought the property at 80 Beach Drive in late 2007 for a record price of $4.25 million. Real estate agents expect the May 9 auction to start with a bid of $3.5 million.

The house has a wide open plan living area and an undercover front balcony. The entrance is at 80 Beach Drive.

Cricket is a sport played all over the world. A list of the best cricket photos from 2014 was chosen, and Matthew Lewis won with a picture of Dwayne Bravo catching a ball. Other photos on the list show ordinary people, like children sorting trash in Bangladesh and a club player trying to catch a ball in Kent.

Robbie Fowler is one of the best strikers in Premier League history. Only five players have scored more goals than his 162. He started his career at Anfield in 1993 and became a goalscoring sensation. He also played for Leeds and Manchester City. He won 26 caps playing for England.

Fowler couldn't resist picking his all-star team from players who played during his time. He picked a starting eleven, including a Dutch striker who is a bit of a debate!

Peter Schmeichel

A group of people dumped 40 tonnes of industrial waste on the side of a road in a village in Suffolk. Police say this is the worst fly-tipping they have seen in almost 30 years. The waste was moved using three tractors and trailers. Cleaning up the rubbish will cost the public thousands of pounds.

Perhaps it was the excitement of the Grand National, but this horse fell at the first hurdle after wandering into thick mud. It was not Becher's Brook - one of Aintree's most famous fences - but the horse, Cody, found himself stuck in a bog in Belvedere, south-east London. Rescue workers climbed into the watery ditch to help the distressed animal to safety on Friday afternoon. Animal rescue experts spent more than an hour rescuing Cody after he wandered into the bog. Cody was covered head to hoof in mud after being dragged to safety, but - despite being shaken by the ordeal - was otherwise unharmed.

Council bosses were embarrassed after a recycling leaflet could not be recycled. The leaflet was attached to green bins and told people what could be recycled. However, a note on it said, "This is not recyclable."

Earlier this year, residents were named as some of the best recyclers in England. According to government figures, Stratford District Council was in the top ten for recycling and composting for the second year running.

Perth Glory fans set off flares during a 3-0 loss to Sydney FC. Police charged two teenagers after a 13-year-old boy suffered burns to his leg. A 16-year-old from Bicton has been charged with causing serious harm and using flares. He will appear in court on May 6. A 15-year-old from Palmyra has also been charged with causing serious harm. He will appear in court on May 8.

Roberto Martinez has ruled Darron Gibson out for the rest of the season. The Everton midfielder injured his metatarsal in a game against Queens Park Queens last month. Martinez had hoped Gibson could play in the final seven games, but now says that is impossible. It is a blow for the team, but Martinez says Gibson does not need surgery to recover.

A 20-year-old man with autism left his home in Brooklyn, New York, 44 days ago and never returned. He told his family he was going for a walk near his house on February 17. His family searched the area because his disability made it hard for him to understand spoken language. On Friday, police found his body in a creek at the Marine Park Golf Club, which is about two miles from his home.

An imam was shot and killed on a street. Police think the killing might be related to terrorism. The imam, Abdul Hadi Arwani, had just been replaced at his mosque by a new preacher. This new preacher, Hassan Anyabwile from Trinidad and Tobago, was involved in an attempted coup 25 years ago. Abdul Hadi was 48 years old. He was found dead in a car in Wembley. He had gunshot wounds to his chest. People who knew him said he was "the most peaceful man you could ever wish to meet." He had a dispute with his former workplace, the An-Noor mosque in Acton.

Everton wants to keep player Darron Gibson on a new contract this summer. The team's manager, Roberto Martinez, said on Thursday that Gibson will miss the last seven games of the season because of a foot injury. Martinez does not think Gibson needs an operation and expects him to be fit for the start of next season.

Gibson, who plays for the Republic of Ireland, has had a hard time recently. He previously tore a ligament in his knee. His spot on the team might be in danger because Everton is also interested in another player, Tom Cleverley, for the summer.

Bradley Neil was not happy to be the one telling Augusta that Jordan Spieth played well. While the 21-year-old American was doing great, the 19-year-old Scot was having a hard time. Neil got to play in the Masters after winning the Scottish Boys Championship in 2013 and the British Amateur Championship last year. He finished the tournament 13 over par. Even though he is still an amateur, world number one Rory McIlroy thinks he will be great once he turns professional.

Danny Willett shouted at a rules official during the Masters on Thursday. The official was sitting in a golf cart about 60 yards away. Willett was angry because his second shot rolled across the putting green, leaving him facing a difficult next shot. He yelled, "Of anyone you should know the rules!" spectators heard him clearly.

Bradley Neil, a 19-year-old Scot, missed the cut at the Masters in his first attempt. He shot rounds of 78 and 79, finishing 13 over par. Despite the tough start, he finished with a birdie on the 18th hole. Neil called the experience a great learning opportunity but admitted he needs to work much harder to compete with the world's best. He played alongside 1988 Masters winner Sandy Lyle.

Sadie the German Shepherd is a musical dog who loves playing the piano instead of fetching sticks. She was filmed in Alberta, Canada, turning on an electric organ with her nose and sitting down to play. Sadie uses her front paws to hit the keys while her back legs rest on the stool. She plays a song with clashing notes and no set rhythm. After she starts confidently, she stops and looks at the camera. Her owner asks, "Oh, did you make a mistake?"

Police are angry at drivers who played football on the M25 motorway while stuck in traffic. A serious motorbike crash between junctions four and five in Orpford, Kent forced the road to close. An air ambulance needed to land to help the injured rider. However, while people waited in the traffic jam, some kicked a ball around on the closed part of the motorway.

Rory McIlroy is trying to win the famous green jacket at Augusta to complete a career grand slam. He is currently the world number one, but he had a shaky start and shot one-under-par 71. He finished seven shots behind the first-round leader, Jordan Spieth.

McIlroy will have to wait and see if the early leaders make mistakes. He is scheduled to play in the second-to-last group on Friday at 6:48pm with Phil Mickelson and Ryan Moore.

Toto Wolff, who works for Mercedes, does not want to ask the bosses at Mercedes for more money to fight Ferrari. Last time in Malaysia, Ferrari was the best car for the first time in almost two years. This pushed Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg down to second and third place.

Andy Murray is getting married on Saturday. Before he relaxes and prepares for his wedding, he wants to finish some work. He is playing in the final of the Miami Open on Sunday against Novak Djokovic. Whether he wins or loses, he will go straight to the airport after the match to get back for his wedding. Murray beat Tomas Berdych to reach the final. His fiancée, Kim Sears, watched him play in Miami.

Glasgow Warriors are very worried because their star player, Richie Gray, might be sold if their team, Castres, gets relegated from the top league. Gray has one year left on his contract, but he will be let go if the club goes down. Other Scottish players, Johnnie Beattie and Max Evans, are also expected to leave. Gray has not played since February because he hurt his arm. The team is doing poorly and is near the bottom of the table with only 38 points.

Lawrence Dallaglio thinks English clubs are doing badly in Europe because of a problem with French rugby, not because there is a big difference in quality between the English and French leagues. Saracens are the only English team left in the semi-finals. Bath, Northampton, and Wasps were knocked out of the Champions Cup this weekend. Saracens barely beat Racing Metro 12-11. The most worrying loss was Clermont beating Saints 37-5. Saints are the current English champions and were leading the league. Jim Mallinder, their rugby director, said this result shows there is a big gap between the English and French leagues.

Tom Croft has signed a new contract with Leicester. This keeps him at the club despite his injury problems. He hurt his shoulder in a recent game and needs surgery. He has had other serious injuries in the past, including a broken neck in 2012 and a knee injury last season. Because of this latest injury, he will likely miss the World Cup.

Derbyshire wicketkeeper Tom Poynton has signed a new one-year contract. The 25-year-old missed the entire 2014 season because he was in a road accident that killed his father, Keith. He had an ankle operation but recovered in time for the new season.

Rangers have promised to investigate claims that Mike Ashley now owns the club's badges. Reports on social media on Thursday suggested the Newcastle United owner is the official owner of the "Light Blues" trademarks, including the "Ready" badge and mascot Broxi Bear. Ashley received security over these icons and logos as part of a £5million loan given to the previous Rangers board in January.

Ferrari's technical director, James Allison, thinks Mercedes will probably be the fastest team in China this weekend. Last time in Malaysia, Mercedes' streak of winning was broken by Sebastian Vettel, who deservedly took the victory. This was Ferrari's first win in almost two years, and it gave hope that the reigning champion Lewis Hamilton and his teammate Nico Rosberg might not win every race. Vettel won the second race of the season in Malaysia last month, beating both Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg from the Mercedes team.

Manchester United fans have been waiting a long time for this. After 16 months, United are back at the top of the Premier League.

For the first time since November 2013, United sit above their rivals Manchester City. This happened because both teams have played the same number of games, and City lost 2-1 to Crystal Palace on Monday.

United are now just one point ahead of City before their big match on Sunday.

Cristiano Ronaldo will play for Real Madrid against Eibar on Saturday. His yellow card from the game against Rayo Vallecano was removed. He was originally booked after Rayo defender Antonio Amaya brought him down in the box, which would have suspended him for one game. However, La Liga's appeals committee decided the punishment was unfair and allowed him to start.

Sergio Aguero says scoring in a Manchester derby is the best feeling. He has scored six goals against Manchester United and wants to score more. He loves scoring in big games. He once hit the post during a loss to Crystal Palace. Aguero says scoring against United gives him shivers. He has scored six times against them, including one in September 2013 at the Etihad.

Lazio is playing well. They won against Napoli on Wednesday and went to the Coppa Italia final. They beat Napoli 2-1 in total. Now they will play Juventus on June 7. A player named Mauricio took a picture of the happy fans with a selfie stick.

Hector Bellerin had a great first year at Arsenal this season. Because he played so well, people are already saying he might move back to Barcelona. The 20-year-old left Barcelona four years ago to get into the first team faster. Now, Barcelona fans want him to return because they think he is the best player to replace Dani Alves if the Brazilian leaves.

Real Madrid's James Rodriguez has been very valuable to the team this season. Spanish newspaper Marca says the Colombian player is "worth his weight in gold." Since moving from Monaco to Real Madrid for £60 million last summer, Rodriguez has settled in well. Marca reports that Real Madrid wins 80% of their games when Rodriguez plays, but only 58% when he is not in the team. Meanwhile, newspaper AS is focusing on Cristiano Ronaldo's appeal.

Eden Hazard thinks Chelsea will win the Premier League title. He scored a penalty and helped set up a goal for Loic Remy to win the game 2-1 against Stoke. This win gave Chelsea a seven-point lead at the top of the table. Jose Mourinho wants his team to win five games and draw one more, and Hazard believes Chelsea can win the title for the first time in five years.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic was not happy just to score 100 goals for Paris Saint-Germain. He scored two more goals in the same game to make it a hat-trick, bringing his total to 102 goals in just three years. This puts him in second place for the most goals in PSG history, behind only Pedro Pauleta. Pauleta scored 109 goals in 211 games, while Ibrahimovic has scored 102 in only 124 games. After scoring, Ibrahimovic slid across the field on his knees.

Pep Guardiola was not happy after Bayern Munich won the German Cup. The team won on penalties against Bayer Leverkusen, but Guardiola was worried about his team's scoring. He said they have not scored enough goals recently, managing only one in their last three games. He believes the team is missing Franck Ribery and Arjen Robben, who are both injured.

David Luiz is out for at least four weeks because he tore a hamstring during a game against Marseille on Sunday. He posted a picture on Instagram on Wednesday showing a new hairstyle, which suggests he is bored while he recovers.

It is T20 season in India. The best cricket players are getting ready for the Indian Premier League. This is a rich and exciting tournament. Eight teams will play 60 games across 12 places in India over almost seven weeks. They are playing to be champions. The final game will be in Kolkata on May 24.

Tim Sherwood says Aston Villa’s star players are "icing on the cake players." He believes they need to become tougher to avoid relegation. He noted that Queens Park Rangers have more experienced players who are "men." Sherwood wants his team to dig deep to solve their problems before their match on Tuesday.

Christian Benteke scored three goals to give Aston Villa a very important point in a 4-4 draw against QPR. Here is a look at how the players performed on Tuesday night at Villa Park.

Aston Villa played in a 4-4-2 formation with a diamond in the middle. Brad Guzan was the goalkeeper. He had a quiet game and could not do much about the goals, but he caught most of the balls that came his way.

Leandro Bacuna played on the right side. He offered a good attacking option but missed a header that allowed the opponent a free jump.

Ron Vlaar also played and had a difficult time during the match.

Arsenal's young team plays Stoke City at the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday night in a U21 league game.

Jack Wilshere, Mikel Arteta, and Abou Diaby start the match as they recover from injuries. Serge Gnabry and Dan Crowley are also in the starting line-up.

Liam Treadwell has been booked to ride Monbeg Dude in Saturday's Grand National. He won the race in 2009 on Mon Mome, a horse trained by Venetia Williams. The ride became available because the horse's usual jockeys, Tom Scudamore and Paul Carberry, are already riding other horses. Treadwell is pictured celebrating his 2009 win.

Alastair Cook says he feels refreshed after spending the winter at home on his farm. England hopes this break has helped him, but he will have very little time to recover before the rest of the year. Cook will play three Tests in the Caribbean this month and then host New Zealand at home. He will also try to help England regain the Ashes this summer, a trophy England lost 5-0 the last time he was captain in 2013-14.

Nabil Fekir's father, Mohamed, says Arsenal would be the best choice for his son, not Manchester City. He believes Nabil would get more playing time at Arsenal under manager Arsene Wenger, rather than sitting on the bench at City. This comes after Nabil recently split with his agents, who wanted to join City. Fekir is currently playing for Lyon.

Kevin Pietersen is angry at Graham Gooch for commenting on his attempt to return to the England team. Gooch spoke on BBC Radio Five Live on Sunday and praised Pietersen, who has re-signed for Surrey to try and get back into the Test team. Gooch, the former England captain and batting coach, said Pietersen had "wiped the floor with the ECB" during their dispute since 2014.

Jack Wilshere, Mikel Arteta, and Abou Diaby will play for Arsenal's Under 21 team on Tuesday night as they recover from injuries. Steve Gatting's young team will face Stoke City at the Emirates Stadium in a U21 Premier League game. Serge Gnabry and Dan Crowley, a talented young player, are also set to play. Jack Wilshere, who was pictured training with the first team last week, is set to play. Club captain Mikel Arteta should also feature. Wilshere watched Arsenal beat Liverpool 4-1 from the stands on Saturday.

Barcelona won 1-0 against Celta Vigo on Sunday. In the 73rd minute, Jeremy Mathieu scored the only goal. Later, Celta striker Fabian Orellana got angry with Barcelona's Sergio Busquets. Orellana picked up a lump of grass from the ground and threw it at Busquets.

Kevin Pietersen has said the first game of his return to county cricket might be streamed live online. The controversial batsman has re-signed with Surrey this summer to try and get back into the England team. He has not played in the County Championship since 2013, but he will start the season with Surrey on Monday, hoping to impress the selectors and reverse his controversial sacking from last year. The 34-year-old wants to end his England absence, which began after the 2013-14 Ashes series.

Jose Mourinho kept the league's joint-top goalscorer, Diego Costa, on the bench at the start of the game. He only wanted to use Costa if it became absolutely necessary.

However, Chelsea had to use him early. Costa came on at halftime to try and stop the team from losing their lead. Unfortunately, he injured his hamstring just 11 minutes after coming onto the field. He limped off the pitch, having re-aggravated the injury that had kept him out of the recent international games with Spain.

Manchester City believes UEFA will drop its punishment for breaking financial rules this summer. This would let them spend money on big players like Raheem Sterling, Gareth Bale, Kevin de Bruyne, and Ross Barkley. Manager Manuel Pellegrini has had trouble buying players because UEFA limited City to spending £49million per transfer window and kept their total wages at £205million a year.

Brittany Lincicome and Stacy Lewis were tied at the end of the tournament. Lincicome made a great shot on the 18th hole to tie the score. Lewis missed a short birdie putt on the final hole, which sent the two players into a playoff. Lincicome then won the tournament.

Derby County want to hire Sean Dyche to replace Steve McClaren this summer. This is true no matter what division Derby are playing in. McClaren, the former England manager, is likely to leave. He has been linked with Newcastle and Sunderland. Derby are making a strong effort to get Dyche, the Burnley manager. Burnley play Tottenham on Sunday. They are still fighting to stay in the top flight, even though many people expected them to be relegated at the start of the season.

Darren Bent might return to Aston Villa in the summer, even though the club let his contract run down and got rid of him. For now, his main focus is helping Derby get promoted.

Bent was not in the plans of the sacked manager Paul Lambert. However, Rams boss Steve McClaren took a chance and signed him on loan until the end of the season. Now, with Tim Sherwood in charge at Villa Park, the 31-year-old striker is keeping his options open.

Since joining Derby in January, Bent has scored nine goals in 13 games. His goal-scoring has been a big help to Derby, who are hoping to finish at the top of the Championship.

It is very hard to remember a big Premier League game where the managers were such good friends. Tim Sherwood and Chris Ramsey know each other very well. They both know that these 90 minutes at Villa Park could change their careers.

They live close to each other, just 10 minutes apart in Buckinghamshire and Bedfordshire. On Tuesday, they will be only 10 metres apart on the touchline in Birmingham. They are enjoying the pressure.

The result of this match could shape their futures. Ramsey's QPR team is going to Sherwood's Villa. The game is important because it could get QPR out of the bottom three.

Jordan Henderson is not giving up on Liverpool's Champions League hopes. Even though Liverpool are eight points behind Manchester United in fourth place, Henderson believes they can still qualify. He scored a penalty in Saturday's 4-1 loss to Arsenal, but the result left Liverpool's top-four chances in serious doubt. This followed a 2-1 home defeat by Manchester United previously. Despite the difficult situation, Henderson urged his teammates not to give up.

Tim Sherwood has told Aston Villa they need to be strong because their game against QPR is the most important one in years. Villa host QPR on Tuesday. Sherwood says his team does not have the players to "grind out" results. If Villa win, they will move five points clear of the bottom three. However, if QPR wins, Villa will drop back to the bottom of the table. Sherwood stressed how big this match is before it starts. Tim Sherwood (from left to right), Les Ferdinand and Chris Ramsey during their time at White Hart Lane.

Clint Hill thinks the teams fighting to avoid relegation are under a lot of pressure. He believes Rangers can stay up if they keep their cool. Even though Rangers are still in the bottom three, Hill thinks other teams should be worried about them. He scored his first Premier League goal on Tuesday in a 3-3 draw against Aston Villa. This result stopped Rangers from moving out of the relegation zone. Hill celebrated after scoring Rangers' second goal. His header made the score 2-2. Rangers took the lead again, but the other team equalized. Rangers are still two points behind the teams above them in the table.

Burnley manager Sean Dyche has denied reports that he is being considered for the Derby job. Recent stories claimed he could replace Steve McClaren at Newcastle, but Dyche says he is focused on his current role at Turf Moor. He stated, "I am enjoying the challenge here. I am not looking further afield." Despite earning a point in a 0-0 draw with Tottenham, Burnley remains in the relegation zone.

Friends and neighbors. For the next 48 hours, Chris Ramsey and Tim Sherwood will compete to avoid being relegated. As QPR manager, Ramsey believes Sherwood’s Aston Villa are safe from going down, despite their low position. He delivered this verdict based on four years of working with Sherwood at Tottenham. Ramsey believes his friend and neighbor will keep Villa in the Premier League. However, Ramsey will be aggressive when he clashes with his former Tottenham colleague on Tuesday.

Tony Fernandes was very sad after his Queens Park Rangers team lost their lead twice against Aston Villa. Christian Benteke scored three goals for Villa, including one just before the end of the game, which stopped QPR from winning. Matt Phillips had given QPR the lead first, but they could not keep the three points and only got a draw.

Wallace, a 20-year-old defender who plays for Chelsea but is currently on loan at Vitesse Arnhem, was questioned by police on suspicion of a sexual offence. He has been released without being charged.

The player was with Vitesse’s squad for a match against Excelsior, but the club has fined him and he will not play in that game. Wallace has previously been loaned out to Fluminense and Inter Milan since joining Chelsea in January 2013. He was arrested in Arnhem last night.

With five games left in the Championship, the race for promotion is still wide open. Eight teams still have a chance to finish in the top two and go straight up to the Premier League. The play-offs are also still very much up for grabs, as the teams are very closely matched. No matter who gets promoted, there have been some excellent individual performances this season.

Melissa Wilson and her teammates are about to make history. On Saturday, the women's boat race will be held on the same course as the men's race. This is a big change because, for 88 years, women were jeered at while racing. Now, the women and men will race at the same time, giving the women equal importance. Wilson's grandfather, Richard Cowell, 85, is very excited. He cannot travel to watch his granddaughter race for Cambridge, but he will watch the race on television.

Chelsea defender Gary Cahill says captain John Terry will not be bothered by the fans when they play QPR at Loftus Road on Sunday.

In 2011, Terry was involved in a race row with former QPR defender Anton Ferdinand. Although a court cleared him of racially abusing Ferdinand, the Football Association banned him for four matches and fined him £220,000 for using language related to colour.

Anton Ferdinand is no longer at QPR, but his brother Rio might play. Terry's former England partner, Gary Cahill, once called him the "biggest idiot" for how he handled the racism row.

The Oxford University Women's Boat Race team was rescued from the River Thames by the Royal National Lifeboat Institution (RNLI) on Wednesday. The rowers and their cox were training for the Boat Race when they got into trouble in choppy water. Crew members from the Chiswick RNLI station helped them. After the rowers were safely taken back to Putney, the sunken boat was recovered and taken back to Oxford's base.

Wasps will try to overturn a three-week ban for Nathan Hughes. However, the appeal will not be ready in time for him to play against Toulon this weekend.

The club says the incident that knocked out George North was an accident, not foul play. The hearing is next Friday, which is too late for Hughes to play on Sunday.

Jose Mourinho will play Nemanja Matic and Cesc Fabregas against Queens Park Rangers, even though they might miss important games later. Both players are one yellow card away from a suspension. If they get a card against QPR, they will miss the games against Arsenal and Manchester United. However, Mourinho says they will still play on Sunday.

Leeds played well and won 26-12 against Castleford at the Mend-A-Hose Jungle in front of a full house. This was their third game in a row without their captain, Kevin Sinfield, who is leaving at the end of 2015. Even without him, the team, known as the Rhinos, kept winning. They had already beaten Wigan and Catalans Dragons, and now they added Castleford to that list. Young player Ash Handley had a great game against Justin Carney.

Northampton took George North out of their game against Clermont Auvergne on Saturday. The club sent him to see a neurosurgeon. This happened because North, a wing for Wales and the Lions, has now had three scary head injuries in two months. He was knocked unconscious on Friday night when Wasps player Nathan Hughes's knee hit him while he was scoring a try. Northampton decided not to risk North in the big game because of his health.

Tom Lineham scored two tries by catching the ball from the other team. Hull FC won 22-8 against Widnes. This was their second win in a row, their first since last June. Lineham is 22 years old and plays on the wing. He scored a total of three tries in the game. His fast running helped Hull FC win.

A neurologist has told George North to rest for at least one month after he got his third concussion in four months while playing for Northampton last week. The Wales and Lions player will be checked again at the end of April. If doctors are not sure he is ready to play, he might be kept out for longer. Saints doctors will check on him during his rest time. There are worries about his health because it takes less of a hit to cause a concussion the more times a player gets one.

Huddersfield forward Jacob Fairbank will be out for a long time after breaking his ankle and damaging ligaments while playing for Halifax on Easter Monday. The 25-year-old was injured during Halifax's win against Hunslet. Scans show he needs a lot of time to recover. Richard Thewlis, from Huddersfield, said it is a big shame because Fairbank is a popular player.

Jonathan Trott is getting ready for his first Test match in 18 months. He had a difficult time during the Ashes tour. In his first practice match in St Kitts, he failed to score twice. He got out for just two runs after top-edging a pull shot. Earlier, he had been out for a duck by Jimmy Anderson. However, he did score 72 runs in the first practice session. He is expected to open the batting with Alastair Cook in the first Test match in Antigua on Monday.

Ben Stokes bowled well on the first day of England's warm-up game in St Kitts. However, he was happiest about the runs scored by Alastair Cook and Jonathan Trott.

England completely dominated the match against a weak St Kitts & Nevis XI. They bowled the home team out for just 59 runs in 27 overs, and then scored 181 runs for the loss of one wicket in reply. The home batsmen played so poorly that the first innings felt like a practice session. Although Stokes took three wickets for 10 runs, the highlight was Alastair Cook playing well behind square on his way to an unbeaten 95.

Richie Benaud, who was 84, died on Friday. He spent a lot of time in the sun when he was young and later got skin cancer on his forehead and head.

He talked about his illness and treatment very honestly. When he was a boy in Australia, he never wore a hat. He wished he had, saying you learn as you go along. He was having radiation treatment for his cancer.

Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho praised striker Loic Remy after he scored the winning goal in a 2-1 victory over Stoke on Saturday. Remy's goal gave Chelsea three points and moved them closer to winning the Premier League title. However, the team suffered a setback when Diego Costa got injured. Costa left the field with a hamstring problem just 10 minutes after coming back from halftime, and will likely be out for a while.

Louis Smith is a very talented man. He won a medal at the Olympics and even won Strictly Come Dancing. Now, at 25 years old, he is becoming known for something else. He is taking selfies like Kim Kardashian. He takes topless selfies to show off his muscles. He posts these photos on Instagram for his fans to see.

Tottenham are confident that Kyle Walker has not broken his foot. There were fears he might have fractured it after he collided with Kieran Trippier during the 0-0 draw at Burnley on Sunday. A scan on Tuesday showed heavy bruising but no fracture. However, the club plans more tests this week. Walker was given a protective boot to wear.

A man from Queensland, Australia, was called 'the dumbest criminal of the week' after he spat on and wrote on a police forensic van in 2013. Cameron Thomas Philp was near a crime scene in Highgate Hill, Brisbane, when he damaged the vehicle. He went to court and pleaded guilty to damaging police property. He was fined $300 but did not get a criminal record. The police found him because they tested the spit on the van and matched it to his DNA.

Cressida Bonas, 26, is happy being single after splitting from Prince Harry. She is a strong, independent woman. She is also starting her acting career and is the new face of the brand Mulberry. Last year, she wore a black Mulberry dress to the Golden Globes and the BAFTAs.

Chris Tremlett thinks Kevin Pietersen can play Test cricket for England again. He believes former boss Paul Downton was wrong to drop Pietersen last year. Pietersen is playing for Surrey this season after signing a new deal. Tremlett and Pietersen were happy together at The Oval.

Kevin Pietersen says his former teammate Michael Vaughan is the best person to change how England plays cricket. This comes ten years after Vaughan captained England to victory in the 2005 Ashes. Vaughan is the leading candidate to become the director of England cricket. He has stayed away from official ECB roles in the past to focus on media and business, but he has now said he is open to talking about the new job.

March was a great month for Arsene Wenger and Arsenal. They won all four of their Premier League games, which secured their spot in the Champions League. Because of this good form, Wenger won the Manager of the Month award. This was his 14th time winning the award. He has won many fewer than his rival, Sir Alex Ferguson, who has won 27. Wenger first won this award in April 2002, when his team won the league title.

Alec Stewart wants to be the new Director of England Cricket. He made this known after Paul Downton was fired on Wednesday. Stewart played 133 Tests for England and currently runs cricket at Surrey. The England and Cricket Board (ECB) has not asked him yet, but he said he would take the job if they asked. Bookmakers think Michael Vaughan is the most likely choice for the job.

Francis Coquelin is focused on playing for Arsenal and wants to be like the club's great captain, Patrick Vieira. Last week, news reported that a white police officer shot and killed an unarmed Black father of four during a traffic stop in South Carolina. This caused a lot of attention because people believe the officer targeted the man because of his race.

However, a young Black man named Will Stack has posted a video online to disagree with those claims. Stack, who is 22 and in the U.S. Army National Guard, says not all white police officers are bad. A pregnant woman named Jeanetta Riley was fatally shot by two Idaho police officers last July. The 35-year-old mother of three was killed outside a hospital in Sandpoint on the evening of July 8, 2014. According to reports, Riley, who struggled with addiction to meth and alcohol, had threatened to kill herself. Her husband had taken her to the hospital for help. The incident was captured on surveillance video.

A mother of three was shot and killed by her husband in Tulare, California. The husband, Gerardo Tovar, 44, then killed himself. Their 4-year-old daughter found the bodies just after midnight on Saturday. The wife, Georgina Rojas-Medina, 41, was the victim of the shooting.

Researchers say that children who share iPads in class score higher on early literacy tests than those who do not. This is despite the general secretary of the National Association of Head Teachers expressing doubt about using technology in non-IT classes. The study suggests that sharing devices is the most effective way to improve literacy levels.

Hailed as one of the most imaginative minds in history, Dr. Seuss created magical worlds with playful rhymes and kooky illustrations. It seems his words have come to life in the depths of Alaska. This towering structure, 130 miles from Anchorage, was once a two-story home. It was built after a forest fire swept the valley clean of trees. Dr. Seuss fans flock to Alaska to visit this 12-cabin-high structure that looks like one of his illustrations. The owner wanted to see the idyllic valley over the tall trees around their cabin. The structure was abandoned for years, but new owners are now renovating it.

On Sunday during the first IndyCar Grand Prix of Louisiana, a crew member for Dayle Coyne Racing was hurt. Todd Phillips, who changes the front outside tires, was hit by Francesco Dracone's car. Dracone had come in on Lap 25 for tires and fuel, and he spun while leaving his pit box, clipping Phillips' leg. Phillips was taken to the infield care center, where he got stitches for a cut on his leg and was then released.

A sports plane crashed onto a motorway in north-west Germany on Sunday afternoon. The four-seater plane went down near Hatten, Oldenburg, shortly after taking off from a nearby airfield. The male pilot died in the crash. Three passengers were taken to a nearby hospital. One man, who was believed to be co-piloting the Cessna 172, is in a serious condition.

Manchester City captain Vincent Kompany says UEFA's Financial Fair Play rules help rich clubs stay rich, rather than stopping them from going bankrupt.

Last year, City were found to have broken these rules and were fined £50million. They are also limited to a £49million spending budget for this season.

City are debt-free because owner Sheikh Mansour invests a lot of his own money. However, rivals Manchester United are roughly £400million in debt, but still spent £150million on new players this summer.

Kompany believes the rules protect the biggest clubs.

A Colorado Rockies pitcher is taking a break from baseball to care for his son. Right-handed reliever John Axford was put on the family medical emergency list before a game on Sunday. His son, Jameson, was bitten by a rattlesnake in Arizona last month and had surgery on his foot last Monday. Axford celebrated his birthday on April 1 with his two sons.

Egyptian officials left an African football event early because they were offended by a belly dancing performance.

Dina Talaat performed at the opening ceremony of the Confederation of African Football's meeting in Cairo. While the show was happening, delegates from Egypt, including Minister Khaled Abdel Aziz, stayed in a different room inside the hotel. They waited there until the performance ended.

Manchester United beat Manchester City 4-2 at Old Trafford. Sergio Aguero scored first for City, but Ashley Young, Marouane Fellaini, Juan Mata, and Chris Smalling all scored before Aguero scored again. This victory ended City's chances of winning the Barclays Premier League title.

The win inspired many funny images on Twitter. David Moyes is being called a genius for signing Juan Mata and Marouane Fellaini. A picture from the Austin Powers films was also used to make fun of City's bad form.

Researchers watched hidden cameras in a London pub for over 70 hours. They found that modern men prefer talking about their children and personal problems, like relationship or sexual issues, instead of football or typical "pub talk." The study showed that men rarely mentioned football, and women were only discussed occasionally.

Louis van Gaal blamed himself for Manchester United finishing the game with only ten players. He used all his substitutes early, which forced Michael Carrick to come off as a precaution because his calf was tight. Van Gaal said, "It was my error that I gave too much playing time to my substitutes. It wasn't a wise decision." He also said some players did not know they were down to ten men because the crowd was yelling so loudly it was hard to get the message to them.

Three former England rugby players went on a charity trip to the North Pole. While flying out, the landing gear of their plane collapsed. The men said they only felt a small jolt. Bad weather forced a first attempt to land to be cancelled, but they carried on with their journey.

Alan Stubbs praised his Hibs players for their bravery after they beat Hearts 2-0 at Easter Road. This victory moved Hibs back into second place in the Championship. It was their second win in a row, helping them recover from a three-game losing streak. The win also set them up for the Scottish Cup semi-final against Falkirk on Saturday. Stubbs noted that his team had answered critics who questioned their ability to win important matches this season.
